question_text:
Design a Verilog module named dut with the following interface:
- input clk: system clock
- input rst_n: asynchronous, active-low reset
- output reg [63:0] Q: 64-bit registered output

Behavior:
- Asynchronous reset: Whenever rst_n is low, Q must be immediately cleared to 64'h0, independent of clk. When rst_n returns high, normal operation resumes on the next rising edge of clk.
- On each rising edge of clk while rst_n is high, update Q based solely on its previous value as follows (the decision uses the value of Q before the update):
  1) If the least significant bit Q[0] is 0, perform a right shift by one with a 1 inserted at the most significant position:
     - Next Q[63] = 1
     - Next Q[62:0] = previous Q[63:1]
  2) If the least significant bit Q[0] is 1, set the two most significant bits to 0 and shift previous bits [62:1] into [61:0]:
     - Next Q[63:62] = 2'b00
     - Next Q[61:0] = previous Q[62:1]

Notes:
- There are no other inputs or controls; the output is fully determined by clk, rst_n, and Q’s own prior state.
- The update must be purely sequential (registered on clk) with the specified asynchronous reset behavior.

Example progression from reset (rst_n asserted low then released): Q starts at 0, then becomes 0x8000_0000_0000_0000, then 0xC000_0000_0000_0000, eventually all 1s; when Q[0] is 1, the next value becomes 0x3FFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF, and so on per the rules above.

(
  input clk,
  input rst_n,
  output reg [63:0] Q
);


  always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
    if(!rst_n) begin
      Q <= 64'h0;
    end else begin
      if(Q[0] == 1'b0) begin
        Q <= { 1'b1, Q[63:1] };
      end else begin
        Q <= { 2'b00, Q[62:1] };
      end
    end
  end


endmodule

Design a synchronous 64-bit module named dut with the following interface:
- input clk: clock.
- input rst_n: asynchronous active-low reset.
- output reg [63:0] Q.

Behavior:
- Asynchronous reset: Whenever rst_n is 0, Q must immediately be cleared to 64'h0, independent of clk. While rst_n is 0, Q remains 0. When rst_n returns to 1, normal operation resumes on the next rising edge of clk.
- On each rising edge of clk while rst_n is 1, update Q as follows, using the value of Q as it existed just before that clock edge:
  1) Let s be the 6-bit unsigned value Q[5:0] (i.e., s ∈ [0,63]).
  2) Form a 64-bit intermediate value T by shifting Q right by one bit and placing the bitwise NOT of the previous least significant bit into the new most significant position:
     T[63] = ~Q[0], and for i=62..0, T[i] = Q[i+1]. Equivalently, T = {~Q[0], Q[63:1]}.
  3) Set Q to the logical left shift of T by s bits: Q_next = T << s. The left shift must zero-fill from the right; bits shifted out of the top are discarded. When s=0, Q_next = T.

- The update is edge-triggered; no combinational outputs other than the registered Q.
- No rotation is performed in the left shift.
- Example (informative): After rst_n is asserted low, Q=0. On the first rising clk edge after deassertion, Q becomes 64'h8000_0000_0000_0000.

     - dataOut is set to the value at the top of stack (the most recently pushed, not yet popped).
     - That popped storage location is cleared to 4’h0.
     - After the edge, occupancy becomes N-1.
     - EMPTY reflects the post-pop state (EMPTY=(N-1==0)).
     - FULL reflects the pre-pop state (i.e., FULL=FULL_pre).
   - If a push is requested when FULL_pre=1, or a pop when EMPTY_pre=1:
     - No stack contents or occupancy change.
     - dataOut must be 4’hx.

question_text:
Design an RTL module dut with the following interface:
- Inputs: clk (rising-edge clock), rst_n (asynchronous active-low reset), write_en, write_addr[7:0], write_data[5:0], read_en, read_addr[7:0].
- Output: read_data[5:0] (registered).

Behavior:
- Address space: only addresses 0..11 will ever be used for both read and write; behavior for other addresses is not required.
- Storage model: each address holds an 8-bit value (“byte”).
- Asynchronous reset (rst_n=0): immediately set read_data to 0 and clear stored bytes at addresses 0 through 7 to 8’h00. The contents at addresses 8 through 11 are not modified by reset (i.e., they retain their prior, unspecified contents). When rst_n returns high, normal operation resumes on the next clock edge.
- Write: on each rising edge of clk, if write_en is 1, write the byte at write_addr as {2’b00, write_data}. No write occurs when write_en is 0.
- Read: on each rising edge of clk, if read_en is 1, update read_data with the upper six bits of the stored byte at read_addr, i.e., stored_byte[7:2]. If read_en is 0, set read_data to 0 on that clock edge (do not hold the previous value).
- Read/write collision: if a read and a write target the same address on the same rising edge, the read must return the value that was stored before that clock edge (no write-through).

All state changes other than the asynchronous reset occur only on rising edges of clk. Implement exactly this behavior and interface.

Design a module dut that implements a small scratchpad with event-driven ports and an active-low asynchronous reset.

Interface:
- input clk
- input rst_n (active-low, asynchronous)
- Write port: input write_en, input [7:0] write_addr, input [5:0] write_data
- Read port: input read_en, input [7:0] read_addr
- Output: output reg [5:0] read_data

Storage:
- The memory holds 12 locations addressable at indices 0..11. Behavior for addresses outside 0..11 is don’t-care.

Reset behavior (dominates all other actions):
- On the falling edge of rst_n, asynchronously:
  - Clear memory locations 0..7 to zero; locations 8..11 are don’t-care and need not be modified.
  - Drive read_data to 0 immediately.
- No writes or reads occur while rst_n is low.

Write behavior (only when rst_n is high):
- A write of write_data to write_addr must occur on either:
  - The rising edge of write_en (asynchronous to clk), and/or
  - Each rising edge of clk while write_en is high.
- If both events occur, both writes happen with the then-current address/data (effectively redundant when unchanged).

Read/output behavior (only when rst_n is high):
- read_data is a registered output updated only by events:
  - On the rising edge of read_en, set read_data to the stored value at read_addr.
  - On each rising edge of clk while read_en is high, set read_data to the stored value at read_addr.
  - On each rising edge of clk while read_en is low, clear read_data to 0.
- When no qualifying read event has occurred since reset, read_data must be 0.

Assume no additional handshakes or valid flags; only the rules above define behavior.

Design a Verilog module named dut that implements a small register file with the following interface:
- Inputs: clk, rst_n (active-low asynchronous reset), write_en, write_addr[7:0], write_data[5:0], read_en, read_addr[7:0]
- Output: read_data[5:0]

Functional requirements:
- Storage: exactly 12 addressable locations (valid addresses 0–11). Each location stores 8 bits, but only the lower 6 bits are significant. On writes, the 6-bit write_data must be zero-extended to 8 bits before storage. On reads, only the lower 6 bits of the addressed location are returned. Accesses to addresses outside 0–11 are don’t-care and will not be tested.
- Reset (asynchronous, active-low): When rst_n is deasserted low, immediately set read_data to 0 and clear locations 0 through 7 to 0. Locations 8 through 11 must not be modified by reset (their contents are unchanged/don’t-care until written).
- Write: A write occurs when either (a) a rising edge of clk happens while write_en=1, or (b) a rising edge of write_en occurs (asynchronous to clk). On such an event, store the zero-extended write_data into the addressed location (subject to the valid address range).
- Read/output timing: read_data updates to the contents of the addressed location on either (a) a rising edge of clk while read_en=1, or (b) a rising edge of read_en (asynchronous to clk). Additionally, on any rising edge of clk while read_en=0, drive read_data to 0. No other implicit holding or combinational read behavior is required.

No write-through is guaranteed; concurrent read and write to the same address may return the previously stored value.

Design a Verilog module named dut that provides a small edge-enabled memory interface with mixed asynchronous/synchronous behavior.

Interface:
- input clk: system clock (operations on rising edge).
- input rst_n: active-low asynchronous reset.
- input write_en: write strobe.
- input [7:0] write_addr: write address (only values 0–11 are valid).
- input [5:0] write_data: write payload.
- input read_en: read strobe.
- input [7:0] read_addr: read address (only values 0–11 are valid).
- output reg [5:0] read_data: read result.

Required behavior:
- Reset (asynchronous, on falling edge of rst_n):
  - Clear read_data to 0.
  - Clear only memory locations 0 through 7 to 0.
  - Memory locations 8 through 11 must remain unchanged by reset.
- Write:
  - On a rising edge of write_en, write write_data to the addressed location.
  - Additionally, on each rising edge of clk while write_en is high, write write_data to the addressed location.
  - Addresses outside 0–11 are not exercised.
- Read:
  - On a rising edge of read_en, update read_data with the contents of the addressed location.
  - Additionally, on each rising edge of clk while read_en is high, update read_data with the contents of the addressed location.
  - On each rising edge of clk while read_en is low, drive read_data to 0.
- Data width:
  - The stored value is 6 bits; read_data must reflect exactly those 6 bits.
- Concurrent access:
  - If a read and a write target the same address in the same triggering event (e.g., the same rising clk), the read must return the value that was stored before the write.

Implement exactly this interface and behavior.

Design a synchronous scratchpad memory with a 6-bit data path and an 8-bit address bus, controlled by a rising-edge clock and an active-low asynchronous reset.

Interface:
- Inputs: clk, rst_n, write_en, write_addr[7:0], write_data[5:0], read_en, read_addr[7:0]
- Output: read_data[5:0] (registered)

Storage:
- The memory contains exactly 12 addressable entries at addresses 0..11.
- Each entry stores 8 bits. Writes store the 6-bit input zero-extended into the upper 2 bits of the 8-bit entry; reads return only the lower 6 bits of the stored byte.

Reset (asynchronous, active-low):
- On any assertion of rst_n=0, immediately set read_data to 0.
- Also, entries at addresses 0..7 must be cleared to 0 on reset. Entries 8..11 are not initialized by reset (their contents after reset are unspecified until written).

Write (synchronous):
- On each rising edge of clk when rst_n=1 and write_en=1, write the addressed entry with the zero-extended write_data.
- If rst_n=0, writes do not occur.

Read (synchronous, registered, read-before-write):
- On each rising edge of clk when rst_n=1:
  - If read_en=1, update read_data with the lower 6 bits of the addressed entry as it existed before any write on that same edge (read-before-write for same-cycle read/write to the same address).
  - If read_en=0, set read_data to 0.
- On rst_n=0, read_data is 0 as stated above.

Assumptions:
- Only addresses 0..11 will be applied on read_addr/write_addr; behavior for other addresses is not tested.

Implement the module named “dut” matching the exact interface and behavior described.

Design a synchronous, single-port register file with the following interface:
- Inputs: clk, rst_n (active-low asynchronous reset), write_en, write_addr[7:0], write_data[5:0], read_en, read_addr[7:0]
- Output: read_data[5:0]

Behavioral requirements:
1) Addressing range: Only addresses 0–11 will be presented on write_addr/read_addr. Behavior for other addresses is not required.
2) Reset: On the falling edge of rst_n, the storage locations at addresses 0–7 shall be cleared to 8'b00000000, and read_data shall be driven to 6'b000000. Locations 8–11 are not modified by reset. While rst_n is low, no writes or reads take effect.
3) Write: On each rising edge of clk when rst_n is high and write_en=1, write the value {2'b00, write_data} into the location indexed by write_addr. If write_en=0, no write occurs.
4) Read and output driving: On each rising edge of clk when rst_n is high:
   - If read_en=1, update read_data to the least significant 6 bits of the stored 8-bit value at read_addr.
   - If read_en=0, drive read_data to 6'b000000 (do not hold the previous value).
5) Simultaneous read/write: If read_en and write_en are both 1 in the same clock edge, the read must return the value that was stored at read_addr before any write on that edge (i.e., no write-through or bypassing).

Implement the module with the exact I/O names and widths specified. Timing behavior must be strictly as described above.

Design a synchronous memory with partial reset and width adaptation.

Module interface:
- input clk
- input rst_n (active-low, asynchronous)
- input write_en
- input [7:0] write_addr
- input [5:0] write_data
- input read_en
- input [7:0] read_addr
- output reg [5:0] read_data

Behavior:
- Storage is an internal 12-word memory addressed 0..11. Each word stores 8 bits. The testbench guarantees read_addr and write_addr are always within 0..11.
- Reset (asynchronous, active-low): When rst_n is asserted low, immediately:
  - read_data becomes 0.
  - Only locations 0..7 are cleared to 0x00.
  - Locations 8..11 are left unchanged (their contents are not modified by reset).
- Normal operation (rst_n high):
  - Write: On each rising edge of clk, if write_en=1, write write_data to the addressed word, zero-extending to 8 bits (i.e., the upper two bits of the stored word become 0).
  - Read: On each rising edge of clk, if read_en=1, update read_data with the least significant 6 bits of the addressed word. If read_en=0, update read_data to 0 on that edge.
- Simultaneous read/write: If read_en and write_en are both 1 on the same rising edge and the addresses are the same, the read must return the contents that existed before the write (read-before-write behavior). If the addresses differ, each operation applies to its own address.
- Timing: There are no combinational reads; read_data changes only on clk rising edges or when rst_n is asserted low.

Implement the module named dut that satisfies the above exactly.

module dut
(
  input clk,
  input rst_n,
  input write_en,
  input [7:0] write_addr,
  input [5:0] write_data,
  input read_en,
  input [7:0] read_addr,
  output reg [5:0] read_data
);

  reg [7:0] mem [0:11];
  integer i;

  always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
    if(!rst_n) begin
      read_data <= 6'b0;
      for(i=0; i<8; i=i+1) begin
        mem[i] <= 8'b0;
      end
    end else begin
      if(write_en) begin
        mem[write_addr] <= { 2'b0, write_data };
      end 
      if(read_en) begin
        if(write_en && (write_addr == read_addr)) begin
          read_data <= mem[read_addr][5:0];
        end else begin
          read_data <= mem[read_addr][5:0];
        end
      end else begin
        read_data <= 6'b0;
      end
    end
  end

Design a synthesizable, purely combinational Verilog module that implements a write-through lookup buffer.

Module requirements:
- Name: dut
- Ports:
  - input wire [7:0] addr
  - output reg [15:0] dout

Internal state:
- Declare an internal 256-entry memory named mem: reg [15:0] mem [0:255].
- In a single initial block, set:
  - mem[0] = 16'hA0A0;
  - mem[1] = 16'hB1B1;
  - mem[2] = 16'hC2C2;
  - mem[3] = 16'hD3D3;
  All other locations may be unspecified at power-up.

Behavior (must be combinational, no clock/reset):
- Use exactly one always @(*) block to both update mem and drive dout.
- On any change of addr, perform a write-first update to the addressed location and an immediate read:
  1) Write mem[addr] with the 16-bit value formed by zero-extending addr: {8'h00, addr}.
  2) Then assign dout the current contents of mem[addr] after this update.
- This write-then-read must occur within the same combinational evaluation (no latency). Consequently, for any addr, dout must immediately equal {8'h00, addr}.
- Subsequent accesses to the same address must observe the updated value; addresses 0–3 will be overwritten upon first access.

Constraints:
- Use blocking assignments inside the combinational block to ensure write-before-read semantics.
- Drive dout only from mem[addr]; do not compute dout directly from addr outside the memory read.
- Do not add ports, additional procedural blocks, or auxiliary registers/wires beyond those specified.

Your solution will be tested for all 8-bit addr values and for proper initialization and overwrite behavior.

Design a Verilog module named dut that models a 256×16 single-port memory with asynchronous, write-first behavior tied to an address input.

Interface:
- input addr[7:0]
- output dout[15:0]

Requirements:
- Internally, the module contains persistent storage for 256 words of 16 bits each.
- At time 0 (simulation initialization), the following locations must be preloaded:
  - mem[0] = 16'hA0A0
  - mem[1] = 16'hB1B1
  - mem[2] = 16'hC2C2
  - mem[3] = 16'hD3D3
  All other locations may be left uninitialized.
- There is no clock, reset, enable, or write data input. The memory is implicitly written whenever addr is observed.
- On any change of addr (combinational sensitivity), the module must:
  1) Write the value {8'h00, addr} into the memory at index addr.
  2) Immediately drive dout with the content stored at index addr after this write (i.e., write-first behavior, zero latency).
- Only the addressed location is modified; all other locations retain their previous contents.
- If addr selects one of the preinitialized locations (0–3), that location is overwritten as described above, and dout must reflect the newly written 16'h00XX value (XX = addr).

Assume addr is always a stable 8-bit 0/1 value. The design must be purely combinational with respect to addr and produce the write-through value on dout in the same simulation delta cycle as the address change.

Design a parameterless Verilog module named dut that exposes:
- input: addr[7:0]
- output: dout[15:0] (driven as a reg)

Internally, declare a 256-entry 16-bit storage array named mem of type reg [15:0] mem [0:255]. At time zero, initialize only the first four entries exactly as:
- mem[0] = 16'hA0A0
- mem[1] = 16'hB1B1
- mem[2] = 16'hC2C2
- mem[3] = 16'hD3D3
All other locations may be left uninitialized.

Behavioral requirement (purely combinational, no clock or reset):
- On any change of addr, the design must immediately perform a write to mem at index addr with the 16-bit value whose upper 8 bits are zero and lower 8 bits equal to addr (i.e., {8'h00, addr}).
- In the same combinational evaluation, dout must reflect mem[addr] as seen after that write (read-after-write in the same evaluation; no additional latency). Thus, for any addr value X, dout must immediately be 16'h00XX.

Additional constraints:
- No additional inputs/outputs or timing controls may be introduced.
- Do not infer latches; the logic must be fully combinational with immediate response to addr changes.
- The storage array must be exactly 256 entries of 16-bit width and named mem.
- Repeated presentation of the same addr must still perform the described write, overwriting any prior contents (including the initialized values for addresses 0–3).

Implement only the described interface and behavior.

Design a combinational read-only lookup module named dut with the following interface:
- input addr[7:0]
- output dout[15:0]

Internally, the module conceptually contains a 256-entry ROM (indices 0 to 255), each entry 16 bits wide. The read address is derived by appending a zero as the least significant bit to addr, i.e., index = {addr, 1’b0} (equivalently, addr shifted left by 1). On any change of addr, dout must update combinationally in the same cycle to the ROM word at that index. No clock, reset, or handshaking signals are used, and no latches or sequential elements are permitted.

ROM initialization:
- Address 0 → 16’hA0A0
- Address 1 → 16’hB1B1
- Address 2 → 16’hC2C2
- Address 3 → 16’hD3D3
All other ROM locations are unspecified and may be ignored by the grader.

Address range and correctness:
- The testcases will only supply addr values in the range 0 to 127 inclusive, ensuring the computed index {addr, 1’b0} lies within 0 to 254.
- Only combinational behavior is graded; reads must reflect the current addr with no delay.

Examples (for clarity):
- addr = 8’h00 → index = 9’h000 → dout = 16’hA0A0
- addr = 8’h01 → index = 9’h002 → dout = 16’hC2C2

Implement the module to satisfy the above behavior and interface exactly. Any behavior for addr > 8’h7F or ROM indices beyond those defined is unspecified and will not be tested.

Design a combinational read-only lookup module as follows:

Interface:
- Module name: dut
- Inputs: addr[7:0]
- Outputs: dout[15:0]

Behavior:
- Internally, there is a 256-entry table of 16-bit words addressed from 0 to 255.
- At simulation time 0, initialize the table so that:
  - location 0 = 16'hA0A0
  - location 1 = 16'hB1B1
  - location 2 = 16'hC2C2
  - location 3 = 16'hD3D3
  All other locations must remain uninitialized (retain their simulator default), and the design must not write to the table thereafter.

- The output is an asynchronous (combinational) read from the table at an effective address computed by multiplying the input addr by 2 (i.e., append a zero as the least-significant bit of addr). Formally, for any addr in the range 0 to 127 inclusive, dout must equal the 16-bit value stored at table address (2*addr).

- The output must reflect changes to addr with zero cycles of latency and without requiring any clock or reset. No additional state or sequencing is permitted; reading does not modify the table.

- For addr values outside 0–127 or for table locations that were not initialized, the behavior is unspecified and may reflect the underlying uninitialized storage.

Implement the module to meet the exact I/O and timing described above.

Design a module named dut that implements an asynchronous, combinational ROM lookup.

Interface:
- Input: addr[7:0] (8-bit unsigned)
- Output: dout[15:0] (16-bit unsigned)

Behavior:
- The module contains a 256-word by 16-bit read-only memory, indexed 0 to 255.
- The output must be a purely combinational function of addr (no clock, no latency).
- To form the ROM index W from addr, append a single 0 bit as the least significant bit of addr (i.e., W = {addr, 0}). This corresponds to doubling the numeric value of addr. The output is the 16-bit word stored at ROM[W].
- Valid input range: addr ∈ [0, 127]. For inputs outside this range, behavior is don’t-care and will not be tested.

Initialization:
- The ROM must be pre-initialized with the following 16-bit values at the specified word indices:
  - ROM[0] = 16’hA0A0
  - ROM[1] = 16’hB1B1
  - ROM[2] = 16’hC2C2
  - ROM[3] = 16’hD3D3
- All other locations may be left unspecified.

Timing and assumptions:
- dout must update immediately to reflect any change on addr (no registers, no inferred latches).
- Assume addr is always a valid 8-bit 0/1 value (no X/Z).

Examples (using W = {addr, 0}):
- addr = 8’h00 → W = 9’h000 → dout = 16’hA0A0
- addr = 8’h01 → W = 9’h002 → dout = 16’hC2C2

Implement only the described behavior and interface.

Design a Verilog module named dut that exposes:
- input addr[7:0]
- output dout[15:0] (reg)

Internally, model a 256×16 read-only memory whose contents are only partially defined at time 0:
- mem[0] = 16'hA0A0
- mem[1] = 16'hB1B1
- mem[2] = 16'hC2C2
- mem[3] = 16'hD3D3
All other locations are left uninitialized (their values are not constrained). No memory writes occur after time 0.

Behavior (no clock, no reset):
- The module must remember the last address value it used to update dout.
- Whenever the current addr is provably different from that remembered address, update both:
  - dout := mem[addr]
  - remembered address := addr
- If the current addr is the same as the remembered address, do not change dout or the remembered address; dout must hold its previous value.
- Use 4-state simulation semantics for comparisons: if the comparison result is unknown (e.g., because the remembered address or addr contains X/Z), the module must not perform an update in that evaluation.
- There is no additional latency: when an update condition is satisfied, dout changes immediately (combinationally).

Initialization and undefined behavior:
- At time 0, the remembered address is not initialized, and dout is not driven to any defined value. Until a definitive addr change relative to the remembered address can be established (under 4-state semantics), dout may remain undefined.

Implement exactly the above interface and behavior without adding clocks or resets.

Design a module dut that exposes:
- input addr: 8-bit address
- output dout: 16-bit registered output

Inside the module, instantiate a 256×16 read-only table mem indexed by addr. Initialize its first four entries exactly as:
- mem[0] = 16'hA0A0
- mem[1] = 16'hB1B1
- mem[2] = 16'hC2C2
- mem[3] = 16'hD3D3
All other mem locations are left unspecified (don’t-care) and must not be written after initialization.

Behavioral requirements:
- There is no clock or reset. The design continuously monitors addr and must remember the last observed address internally (a stored “previous address” state).
- Whenever addr becomes different from the remembered address, immediately (combinationally) update dout to mem[addr] and update the remembered address to the current addr.
- If addr is equal to the remembered address, do not update dout or the remembered address; both must retain their previous values.
- At power-up, the remembered address and dout may be unknown/don’t-care until the first qualifying update as defined above.
- Only the change of addr relative to the remembered address may cause dout to change. No other side effects are allowed.

Interface and structural constraints:
- Use exactly the specified ports and widths; add no additional I/O.
- The lookup must be implemented with a 256-deep 16-bit reg array named mem initialized in an initial block as specified.
- Implement the update logic in a single combinational process; no clocked logic is permitted.

Your solution must satisfy the above behavior precisely for all addr values 0–255.

Design a combinational RTL module named dut that filters ROM reads based on changes to the address input.

Interface:
- input addr[7:0]
- output dout[15:0] (registered output)

Functionality:
- Internally, the module contains a 256×16 read-only memory (ROM) addressed by addr. The ROM is asynchronously read.
- The ROM must be pre-initialized as follows:
  - mem[0] = 16'hA0A0
  - mem[1] = 16'hB1B1
  - mem[2] = 16'hC2C2
  - mem[3] = 16'hD3D3
  - All other locations may be left uninitialized (don’t-care).
- The module must remember the last observed 8-bit address value. Only when addr changes to a different value than the remembered one shall the module:
  - drive dout with the ROM word at the new addr, and
  - update the remembered address to this new addr.
- If addr does not change value, dout must hold its previous value exactly (no spurious updates).
- There is no clock, reset, or enable. Behavior is purely combinational with state retained across time to detect address changes.
- Power-up behavior: the remembered address and dout are unspecified before the first detected change; it is acceptable for dout to remain unknown until a change in addr is observed. Do not force any initial read based solely on the power-up addr value.

Constraints:
- Do not add ports.
- Reading from uninitialized ROM entries yields unconstrained values.

Your task is to implement dut so it satisfies the above semantics under standard 4-state Verilog simulation.

Design a combinational module named dut that exposes a single asynchronous read-only port into a 256×16 memory.

Interface:
- input [7:0] addr: 8-bit address, valid range 0–255.
- output reg [15:0] dout: 16-bit data output.

Behavior:
- The memory has 256 locations (0 to 255), each 16 bits. At time 0, initialize:
  - mem[0] = 16'hA0A0
  - mem[1] = 16'hB1B1
  - mem[2] = 16'hC2C2
  - mem[3] = 16'hD3D3
  All other locations are unspecified (don’t care for testing).
- The read is asynchronous with zero latency, but is intentionally sensitive only to the upper 7 address bits. Specifically:
  - When any bit of addr[7:1] changes, dout must immediately update to the value stored at the memory location indexed by the full 8-bit addr at that moment.
  - When only addr[0] toggles (with addr[7:1] unchanged), dout must not change and must retain its previous value (no update, no glitch).
- There is no clock or reset. dout’s value before the first change on addr[7:1] is don’t care.

Clarifications:
- The effective address used for the read on an update is the current full addr[7:0].
- Example expectation: Starting at addr=8'h00, dout=A0A0. Changing addr to 8'h01 (only bit 0 toggles) must keep dout=A0A0. Changing addr to 8'h02 (bit 1 toggles) must update dout to C2C2; changing to 8'h03 (only bit 0 toggles) must keep dout=C2C2.

Implement only the described module and interface.

Design a Verilog-2001 module named dut that implements a read-only lookup from an internal 256×16 storage with a specific update behavior tied only to the upper address bits.

Interface:
- input [7:0] addr: 8-bit address (0–255).
- output reg [15:0] dout: 16-bit data output.

Behavior:
- At time 0, initialize the internal storage so that:
  - location 0 = 16'hA0A0
  - location 1 = 16'hB1B1
  - location 2 = 16'hC2C2
  - location 3 = 16'hD3D3
  The contents of other locations are not specified or tested.
- The output must reflect a lookup of the current full 8-bit address (i.e., dout equals the stored word at index addr) without any clock.
- Timing/edge condition: dout must update immediately whenever any bit of addr[7:1] changes. If addr changes only in bit 0 (addr[0]) while addr[7:1] remain constant, dout must not change at that time and must hold its previous value. Upon a subsequent change to any bit of addr[7:1], dout must then immediately reflect the stored word at the current full addr, including the possibly changed addr[0].
- No write ports or clocks/resets are present; the module is purely read-only with the above update condition. Continuous updating on addr[0] changes is explicitly disallowed.

Constraints:
- Do not add extra I/O.
- The behavior will be verified by sequences where addr toggles only in bit 0 versus toggling any of bits [7:1].

Implement dut to meet these requirements precisely.

Design a Verilog RTL module named dut with the following interface:
- input wire [7:0] addr
- output reg [15:0] dout

Internally, the module contains a 256×16 read-only lookup table mem indexed by addr. Initialize the table with:
- mem[0] = 16'hA0A0
- mem[1] = 16'hB1B1
- mem[2] = 16'hC2C2
- mem[3] = 16'hD3D3
No other locations are explicitly initialized; their values are not checked by the tests.

Behavioral requirements:
- There is no clock or reset. The output updates asynchronously.
- When the upper 7 bits of the address (addr[7:1]) change, dout must immediately take the value stored at mem[addr] for the full 8-bit address present at that moment.
- A change to only the least-significant bit (addr[0]) must not cause any reevaluation or change of dout. In other words, if addr[7:1] remains constant while addr[0] toggles, dout must hold its prior value until a subsequent change of addr[7:1].
- There are no writes to mem and no side effects; the module only reads mem to drive dout.
- Timing: updates described above occur without clocked latency; do not introduce edge-sensitive logic or additional handshaking.

Notes:
- Tests will probe addresses 0–3 to verify initialization and will also toggle addr[0] while holding addr[7:1] constant to confirm the specified “update on addr[7:1] change only” behavior.
- Do not add any extra I/O ports.

Implement the module to satisfy the exact behavior described.

Design a Verilog module named dut with the following interface:
- input clk: clock, rising-edge triggered.
- input rst_n: asynchronous active-low reset.
- input [7:0] data_in: unsigned input sample.
- input valid_in: input-sample qualifier.
- output reg valid_out: output qualifier.
- output reg [9:0] data_out: unsigned output sum.

Behavior:
- Define ready_add as (~valid_out) OR valid_in (evaluated in the same clock cycle as the registers update).
- A sample is “accepted” on a clock edge if ready_add is 1. If ready_add is 0, all state holds and no sample is accepted.
- Maintain a 2-bit counter count that:
  - is cleared to 0 on reset,
  - increments by 1 on each accepted sample,
  - and is cleared to 0 on the same cycle that the 4th accepted sample occurs.
- Maintain a running accumulation over groups of exactly four accepted samples:
  - On the first accepted sample of a group (count == 0), set data_out to data_in.
  - On the 2nd–4th accepted samples, set data_out to data_out + data_in.
  - Arithmetic is unsigned and wraps modulo 1024.
- valid_out is asserted for exactly one clock cycle coincident with the acceptance of the 4th sample in a group; otherwise it is 0.
- Reset behavior (asynchronous on rst_n low): count, data_out, and valid_out are cleared to 0. After reset deasserts, operation proceeds per the rules above.

Timing notes:
- All registers update on clk’s rising edge.
- The definition of acceptance uses ready_add as specified, without additional handshakes.

Implement exactly this behavior.

Design a synchronous RTL module dut with the following interface:
- Inputs: clk (clock), rst_n (asynchronous active-low reset), data_in[7:0], valid_in.
- Outputs: data_out[9:0], valid_out.

Behavior:
- On rst_n deasserted (low), asynchronously clear internal state: data_out := 0 and valid_out := 0.
- State updates occur on each rising edge of clk when not in reset.
- The module processes data_in in “runs” of exactly 4 accepted cycles. Define an accepted cycle as any cycle in which the module advances its accumulator. The advancement policy is:
  - After asserting a result (valid_out = 1), the next cycle advances only if valid_in = 1; otherwise it stalls (no counter/accumulator update, valid_out = 0).
  - In all other cycles, the module advances unconditionally (i.e., it does not require valid_in).
- Accumulation within a run:
  - On the first accepted cycle of a run, set data_out := zero-extended data_in.
  - On each subsequent accepted cycle in the same run, update data_out := data_out + data_in (10-bit arithmetic, no saturation).
- When the 4th accepted cycle of a run is processed, assert valid_out = 1 for exactly that cycle (a single-clock pulse). In that same cycle, data_out must equal the sum of the 4 accepted data_in samples of the run. In all other cycles, valid_out = 0.
- After producing the pulse, automatically reset the run (accumulator continues as specified by the advancement policy).
- On reset release, the first run begins immediately without waiting for valid_in.

Assume data_in values are arbitrary; sums may use full 10 bits.

Design a synchronous RTL module dut with the following interface:
- Inputs: clk (rising-edge), rst_n (asynchronous active-low), data_in[7:0], valid_in.
- Outputs: data_out[9:0], valid_out.

Behavior:
- After reset deassertion, initialize data_out=0 and valid_out=0, and start a new group.
- The module processes groups of exactly four accepted samples. A sample is accepted on a clock edge if (valid_out==0) OR (valid_in==1). If a sample is not accepted on a clock edge, all internal state and data_out hold their values.
- On an accepted sample:
  - If it is the first sample of the current group, set data_out to zero-extended data_in (bits [9:8]=0, bits [7:0]=data_in).
  - Otherwise, add zero-extended data_in to data_out.
- When the fourth sample of a group is accepted, the group completes. On the clock edge that processes this fourth sample:
  - data_out must hold the final 10-bit sum of the four zero-extended samples,
  - valid_out must be asserted high for exactly one cycle,
  - the next sample index resets to the first sample of the next group.
- While valid_out is high (the single-cycle completion pulse), the next group’s first sample is accepted only if valid_in==1 on that same cycle; otherwise, no state changes that cycle, valid_out deasserts on the next cycle, and then samples are accepted unconditionally again (per the acceptance rule above).
- On any cycle without an accepted sample, valid_out must be 0 (except for the completion pulse cycle itself).

Additionally, maintain an internal 10-bit register that mirrors data_out whenever data_out updates and is preserved by synthesis using a “keep” attribute.

Timing: All state updates occur on clk’s rising edge; rst_n asynchronously clears state when low.

Design a synchronous RTL module dut with the following interface:
- Inputs: clk (clock), rst_n (asynchronous active-low reset), data_in[7:0], valid_in.
- Outputs: valid_out (1-bit), data_out[9:0].

Behavior (all sequential updates occur on the rising edge of clk; combinational conditions are evaluated from values present before the edge):
- Reset: When rst_n is low, asynchronously clear valid_out and data_out to 0, and clear an internal 2-bit counter count to 0.
- Define a combinational readiness signal ready_add that is asserted when either valid_out is deasserted or valid_in is asserted: ready_add = (!valid_out) OR valid_in.
- Define a combinational end condition end_cnt that is asserted when ready_add is high and the counter equals 3: end_cnt = ready_add AND (count == 3).
- valid_out is a single-cycle pulse: on each clock, set valid_out to 1 if end_cnt is true; otherwise set it to 0.
- The 2-bit counter count updates only when valid_out is high on that cycle. If end_cnt is true, reset count to 0; else if valid_out is high, increment count by 1 modulo 4; otherwise hold its value.
- data_out updates only when valid_out is high on that cycle. If count == 0, load data_out with zero-extended data_in (bits [9:8]=0, bits [7:0]=data_in). Otherwise, add data_in to the current data_out with 10-bit wraparound. If valid_out is low, hold data_out.

No additional handshakes or latency beyond what is specified above.

Design a synchronous RTL module named dut with the following interface:
- Inputs: clk, rst_n (active-low asynchronous reset), data_in[7:0], valid_in.
- Outputs: valid_out, data_out[9:0].

Behavior:
- Reset: While rst_n=0, valid_out and data_out must be 0, and all internal state cleared. On rst_n deassertion, normal operation resumes on the next rising edge of clk.
- Define a one-cycle “ready” condition each cycle as: ready = (!valid_out) OR valid_in.
- The module maintains an internal 2-bit index idx (modulo-4), initialized to 0 on reset. On each rising edge of clk:

question_text:
Design a purely combinational, hierarchical adder-like network with the following top-level interface:
- module dut(input [15:0] a, input [15:0] b, input Cin, output [15:0] y, output Co).

Behavior is defined by composing identical 1-bit cells upward through 2-bit, 4-bit, and 8-bit blocks to form the 16-bit top. Bit 0 is the least significant bit (LSB).

1) 1-bit cell semantics (used at every bit position i):
- Inputs: a[i], b[i], Cin_i.
- Outputs: y[i], Cout_i.
- y[i] = 1 if and only if exactly one of {a[i], b[i], Cin_i} is 1; otherwise y[i] = 0.
- Cout_i = 1 if and only if at least two of {a[i], b[i], Cin_i} are 1; otherwise Cout_i = 0.

2) 2-bit block (bits [1:0]): cascade two 1-bit cells from LSB to MSB. Feed Cin to bit 0; connect Cout_0 to Cin of bit 1; export y[1:0] and Cout_1 as Co.

3) 4-bit block (bits [3:0]): cascade two 2-bit blocks. Feed Cin to the lower block [1:0]; connect its Co to the upper block [3:2]; export y[3:0] and the upper block’s Co.

4) 8-bit block (bits [7:0]): cascade two 4-bit blocks. Feed Cin to [3:0]; ripple Co to [7:4]; export y[7:0] and Co.

5) 16-bit top (bits [15:0]): cascade two 8-bit blocks. Feed Cin to [7:0]; ripple Co to [15:8]. Outputs are y[15:0] and the final Co.

There is no clock or reset; outputs must reflect inputs combinationally. Ensure strict bit slicing as specified: lower halves use the lower indices, upper halves use the higher indices, with carries always rippling from lower to higher bits.

question_text:
Design a purely combinational 16-bit adder using a fixed hierarchy of modules. Implement the following modules with exactly these names, ports, and widths:

Top module dut:
- Inputs: a[15:0], b[15:0], Cin
- Outputs: y[15:0], Co
- Internals: declare wire [1:0] Co_temp.
- Instantiate exactly two dut_dependency_2 instances named add8_inst1 and add8_inst2.
  - add8_inst2 computes bits [7:0]: connect a[7:0], b[7:0], Cin to its Cin; drive y[7:0]; connect its Co to Co_temp.
  - add8_inst1 computes bits [15:8]: connect a[15:8], b[15:8]; connect its Cin to Co_temp; drive y[15:8]; connect its Co to dut.Co.

Module dut_dependency_2 (8-bit adder):
- Ports: a[7:0], b[7:0], Cin, y[7:0], Co
- Declare wire Co_temp (1 bit).
- Instantiate exactly two dut_dependency_3 instances named add4_inst1 (upper nibble) and add4_inst2 (lower nibble).
- Connect lower’s Cin to parent Cin and its Co to Co_temp; connect upper’s Cin to Co_temp and its Co to parent Co. Slice bits [3:0] and [7:4] accordingly.

Module dut_dependency_3 (4-bit adder):
- Ports: a[3:0], b[3:0], Cin, y[3:0], Co
- Declare wire Co_temp (1 bit).
- Instantiate exactly two dut_dependency_4 instances add2_inst1 (upper) and add2_inst2 (lower) with the same carry chaining and slicing: [1:0] lower, [3:2] upper.

Module dut_dependency_4 (2-bit adder):
- Ports: a[1:0], b[1:0], Cin, y[1:0], Co
- Declare wire Co_temp (1 bit).
- Instantiate exactly two dut_dependency_5 instances add1_inst1 (upper) and add1_inst2 (lower) with the same chaining.

Module dut_dependency_5 (1-bit full adder):
- Ports: a, b, Cin, y, Co
- Implement as combinational logic: y = (~a & ~b & Cin) | (~a & b & ~Cin) | (a & ~b & ~Cin) | (a & b & Cin); Co = (~a & b & Cin) | (a & ~b & Cin) | (a & b & ~Cin) | (a & b & Cin).

Use named port connections. No clocks, resets, generates, or extra signals.

question_text:
Design a purely combinational, hierarchical ripple-carry adder as follows.

Top module dut:
- Inputs: a[15:0], b[15:0], Cin (1-bit).
- Outputs: y[15:0], Co (1-bit).
- Behavior: Treat a, b, and Cin as unsigned. y is the least-significant 16 bits of a + b + Cin; Co is the carry-out bit of that 17-bit sum. No clocks, resets, or timing dependencies; outputs reflect inputs combinationally.

Hierarchy and required submodules (you must implement all):
1) dut_dependency_2 (8-bit):
   - Ports: a[7:0], b[7:0], Cin -> y[7:0], Co.
   - Built by cascading two dut_dependency_3 instances: lower 4 bits take Cin; upper 4 bits take the lower instance’s Co.

2) dut_dependency_3 (4-bit):
   - Ports: a[3:0], b[3:0], Cin -> y[3:0], Co.
   - Built by cascading two dut_dependency_4 instances similarly (lower half takes Cin; upper half takes lower’s Co).

3) dut_dependency_4 (2-bit):
   - Ports: a[1:0], b[1:0], Cin -> y[1:0], Co.
   - Built by cascading two dut_dependency_5 instances similarly.

4) dut_dependency_5 (1-bit full adder):
   - Ports: a, b, Cin -> y, Co.
   - Behavior: y = parity(a, b, Cin) (odd count of ones); Co = majority(a, b, Cin) (at least two ones).

Top-level composition:
- Instantiate two dut_dependency_2 adders: lower for a[7:0], b[7:0]; upper for a[15:8], b[15:8].
- The lower 8-bit instance’s Cin is the top-level Cin.
- The upper 8-bit instance’s Cin is driven by the lower 8-bit instance’s Co.
- Constraint: In dut, route this inter-stage carry via an internal wire [1:0]; connect the lower Co to this 2-bit wire and connect the upper Cin to the same 2-bit wire without bit slicing.

All outputs are wires; use structural/continuous logic only.

question_text:
Design a purely combinational, hierarchical ripple-carry adder.

Top-level:
- Module name: dut
- Ports: a[15:0], b[15:0], Cin (inputs); y[15:0], Co (outputs)
- Internal wire: Co_temp declared as a 2-bit vector [1:0]
- Instantiate exactly two dut_dependency_2 instances:
  - add8_inst1: connects a[15:8], b[15:8] to y[15:8], Co to top Co; its Cin must be driven by Co_temp (pass the 2-bit vector, do not index it)
  - add8_inst2: connects a[7:0], b[7:0] to y[7:0]; its Cin is Cin; its Co must drive Co_temp (connect to the 2-bit vector, do not index it)

8-bit stage:
- Module name: dut_dependency_2
- Ports: a[7:0], b[7:0], Cin (inputs); y[7:0], Co (outputs)
- Internal wire: Co_temp as a 1-bit scalar
- Instantiate exactly two dut_dependency_3 instances:
  - add4_inst1: upper nibble [7:4], Cin=Co_temp, Co drives module Co
  - add4_inst2: lower nibble [3:0], Cin=Cin, Co drives Co_temp

4-bit stage:
- Module name: dut_dependency_3
- Ports: a[3:0], b[3:0], Cin; y[3:0], Co
- Internal wire: Co_temp as a 1-bit scalar
- Instantiate exactly two dut_dependency_4 instances:
  - add2_inst1: upper bits [3:2], Cin=Co_temp, Co drives module Co
  - add2_inst2: lower bits [1:0], Cin=Cin, Co drives Co_temp

2-bit stage:
- Module name: dut_dependency_4
- Ports: a[1:0], b[1:0], Cin; y[1:0], Co
- Internal wire: Co_temp as a 1-bit scalar
- Instantiate exactly two dut_dependency_5 instances:
  - add1_inst1: bit 1, Cin=Co_temp, Co drives module Co
  - add1_inst2: bit 0, Cin=Cin, Co drives Co_temp

1-bit stage:
- Module name: dut_dependency_5
- Ports: a, b, Cin; y, Co
- Implement a full-adder using only NOT, AND, OR with canonical sum-of-products for the truth table (no +, ^, ?:).

Use named port connections. No clocks, delays, or latches. The output must equal a + b + Cin.

question_text:
Design a purely combinational hierarchical adder using the exact module interfaces below. Do not use clocks, resets, procedural blocks, or arithmetic operators (+, -); only combinational wiring and the specified submodule instantiations.

Top module:
- dut
  - Inputs: a[15:0], b[15:0], Cin
  - Outputs: y[15:0], Co

Submodules (to be implemented and used hierarchically):
- dut_dependency_2: 8-bit adder
  - Inputs: a[7:0], b[7:0], Cin
  - Outputs: y[7:0], Co
- dut_dependency_3: 4-bit adder
  - Inputs: a[3:0], b[3:0], Cin
  - Outputs: y[3:0], Co
- dut_dependency_4: 2-bit adder
  - Inputs: a[1:0], b[1:0], Cin
  - Outputs: y[1:0], Co
- dut_dependency_5: 1-bit full adder
  - Inputs: a, b, Cin (scalars)
  - Outputs: y, Co (scalars)

Functional requirements:
- dut_dependency_5 must implement a 1-bit full adder: for all a,b,Cin∈{0,1}, y = a XOR b XOR Cin, and Co = 1 iff at least two of {a,b,Cin} are 1.
- Each wider adder must be built by instantiating exactly two instances of the next-lower adder, rippling carry from the lower slice to the higher slice:
  - dut_dependency_4: bit 0 feeds bit 1; outputs map to y[0] and y[1].
  - dut_dependency_3: [1:0] feeds [3:2]; outputs map to y[1:0] and y[3:2].
  - dut_dependency_2: [3:0] feeds [7:4]; outputs map to y[3:0] and y[7:4].
- dut must instantiate two dut_dependency_2 blocks:
  - The lower byte a[7:0], b[7:0] with Cin produces the upper half of y: y[15:8].
  - The upper byte a[15:8], b[15:8] with carry-in from the lower byte produces the lower half of y: y[7:0].
  - Co is the carry-out of the upper-byte block.
Thus, y is the byte-swapped sum of a + b + Cin, and Co is the final carry-out.

question_text:
Design a purely combinational 16-bit adder with a byte-swapped sum and a hierarchical ripple-carry structure.

Top module:
- Name: dut
- Ports:
  - input [15:0] a, b
  - input Cin
  - output [15:0] y
  - output Co
- Behavior: Interpret a and b as unsigned. Let S = a + b + Cin computed with full carry ripple from bit 0 to bit 15. Set Co = S[16]. Set y by swapping the two bytes of the 16-bit sum: y[15:8] = S[7:0] and y[7:0] = S[15:8]. Outputs must reflect inputs combinationally (no clocks, latches, or state).

You must implement the following helper modules and use them hierarchically as described:
- dut_dependency_5 (1-bit full adder)
  - Ports: input a, b, Cin; output y, Co
  - Function: y = a ⊕ b ⊕ Cin; Co is the majority of (a, b, Cin).
- dut_dependency_4 (2-bit ripple adder)
  - Ports: input [1:0] a, b, Cin; output [1:0] y, Co
  - Ripple from bit 0 to bit 1: bit 0 uses Cin and produces carry into bit 1. y[0] is the sum of a[0], b[0], Cin; y[1] is the sum of a[1], b[1], and the carry from bit 0; Co is the carry out of bit 1.
- dut_dependency_3 (4-bit ripple adder)
  - Ports: input [3:0] a, b, Cin; output [3:0] y, Co
  - Built as two 2-bit stages: lower [1:0] first with Cin; its carry feeds upper [3:2]. y[1:0] from lower, y[3:2] from upper; Co from upper.
- dut_dependency_2 (8-bit ripple adder)
  - Ports: input [7:0] a, b, Cin; output [7:0] y, Co
  - Built as two 4-bit stages: lower [3:0] first with Cin; its carry feeds upper [7:4]. y[3:0] from lower, y[7:4] from upper; Co from upper.

Top-level dut must connect two dut_dependency_2 blocks so that the lower-byte adder (a[7:0], b[7:0], Cin) produces y[15:8] and its carry-in feeds the upper-byte adder (a[15:8], b[15:8]), which produces y[7:0] and Co.

Example: a=16'h1234, b=16'h0102, Cin=1 => S=17'h01337, y=16'h3713, Co=0.

question_text:
Design a purely combinational, hierarchical ripple-carry adder with a byte-swapped top-level output.

Implement five modules with the exact names and interfaces:
- dut: inputs a[15:0], b[15:0], Cin; outputs y[15:0], Co
- dut_dependency_2: inputs a[7:0], b[7:0], Cin; outputs y[7:0], Co
- dut_dependency_3: inputs a[3:0], b[3:0], Cin; outputs y[3:0], Co
- dut_dependency_4: inputs a[1:0], b[1:0], Cin; outputs y[1:0], Co
- dut_dependency_5: inputs a, b, Cin; outputs y, Co

Functional requirements:
- dut_dependency_5 is a 1-bit full adder: y = a ⊕ b ⊕ Cin; Co = majority(a, b, Cin). It is the only place arithmetic is defined; all wider modules must be structural compositions of smaller ones.
- For each k-bit module (k ∈ {2,4,8}), build it from two (k/2)-bit adders in ripple fashion:
  • The lower (least significant) sub-adder consumes the module’s Cin and produces an internal carry.
  • The higher (most significant) sub-adder consumes that internal carry as its Cin.
  • The module’s y concatenates the lower half result into its lower bits and the higher half result into its higher bits in natural order.
  • The module’s Co is the higher sub-adder’s Co.
- Top-level dut composes two 8-bit adders as above, but its y is byte-swapped:
  • y[15:8] = sum of a[7:0] + b[7:0] + Cin (lower byte result).
  • y[7:0]  = sum of a[15:8] + b[15:8] + carry-out from the lower byte.
  • Co is the carry-out from the upper byte addition.

No clocks, resets, or latches. All outputs must be stable combinational functions of inputs for all 2^33 input combinations.

question_text:
Design a hierarchical 16-bit adder with a specific structure and primitive behavior.

Top module:
- Name: dut
- Ports:
  - input [15:0] a, b
  - input Cin
  - output [15:0] y
  - output Co

Hierarchy and carry chaining:
- dut shall instantiate exactly two 8-bit adders (module dut_dependency_2):
  - Lower 8-bit adder computes y[7:0] from a[7:0], b[7:0], Cin and produces an internal carry.
  - Upper 8-bit adder computes y[15:8] from a[15:8], b[15:8] using the lower adder’s carry as its Cin; its Co drives dut.Co.
- Each dut_dependency_2 shall instantiate exactly two 4-bit adders (module dut_dependency_3) with the same lower-to-upper ripple-carry chaining and MSB/LSB bit slicing ([3:0] then [7:4]).
- Each dut_dependency_3 shall instantiate exactly two 2-bit adders (module dut_dependency_4), similarly chained and sliced ([1:0] then [3:2]).
- Each dut_dependency_4 shall instantiate exactly two 1-bit primitives (module dut_dependency_5), sliced ([0] then [1]) with ripple carry from bit 0 to bit 1.

1-bit primitive behavior (dut_dependency_5):
- Ports: input a, b, Cin; output y, Co.
- Carry-out Co must equal the full-adder carry: (~a & b & Cin) | (a & ~b & Cin) | (a & b & ~Cin) | (a & b & Cin).
- Sum y is a level-sensitive latch with enable = ~Cin:
  - When Cin = 0, y updates to a XOR b.
  - When Cin = 1, y holds its previous value (no clock, no reset; initial value is don’t-care).

No clocks are used elsewhere; all other logic is purely combinational. Ensure exact port widths, names, bit slicing, and carry connections as specified.

question_text:
Design a hierarchical 16-bit adder with a gated-sum bit cell and exact module/port names as specified below.

Top module:
- Name: dut
- Ports: input a[15:0], input b[15:0], input Cin, output y[15:0], output Co
- Behavior: Split a and b into lower [7:0] and upper [15:8] halves. Instantiate exactly two dut_dependency_2 instances:
  - add8_inst2 handles lower 8 bits with Cin, producing y[7:0] and an intermediate carry.
  - add8_inst1 handles upper 8 bits with Cin equal to that intermediate carry, producing y[15:8] and Co.

8-bit submodule:
- Name: dut_dependency_2
- Ports: input a[7:0], input b[7:0], input Cin, output y[7:0], output Co
- Behavior: Cascade two dut_dependency_3 instances:
  - add4_inst2 handles a[3:0], b[3:0] with Cin, producing y[3:0] and an intermediate carry.
  - add4_inst1 handles a[7:4], b[7:4] with Cin equal to that intermediate carry, producing y[7:4] and Co.

4-bit submodule:
- Name: dut_dependency_3
- Ports: input a[3:0], input b[3:0], input Cin, output y[3:0], output Co
- Behavior: Cascade two dut_dependency_4 similarly on [1:0] then [3:2].

2-bit submodule:
- Name: dut_dependency_4
- Ports: input a[1:0], input b[1:0], input Cin, output y[1:0], output Co
- Behavior: Cascade two dut_dependency_5 on bit 0 then bit 1.

1-bit submodule (gated-sum cell):
- Name: dut_dependency_5
- Ports: input a, input b, input Cin, output y, output Co
- Carry-out: Co = (a & b) | (a & Cin) | (b & Cin).
- Sum y is a level-sensitive latch transparent when Cin=0 and holding its previous value when Cin=1. When Cin=0, y equals:
  (~a & ~b & Cin) | (~a & b & ~Cin) | (a & ~b & ~Cin) | (a & b & Cin).

Notes:
- No clocks or resets. Drive all outputs via continuous assignments.
- Do not use generate/loops. Use the exact instance names shown.

question_text:
Design a purely combinational, hierarchical 16-bit adder with the exact module interfaces and structure below.

Top module:
- Name: dut
- Ports: input a[15:0], b[15:0], Cin; output y[15:0], Co.
- Must instantiate exactly two dut_dependency_2 blocks: the lower half consumes a[7:0], b[7:0], Cin and produces y[7:0] and an internal carry; the upper half consumes a[15:8], b[15:8] and that internal carry, producing y[15:8] and final Co.
- Use a single internal wire named Co_temp to connect the halves.

8-bit block:
- Name: dut_dependency_2
- Ports: input a[7:0], b[7:0], Cin; output y[7:0], Co.
- Must instantiate exactly two dut_dependency_3 blocks: lower nibble uses Cin and produces an internal carry; upper nibble uses that carry; outputs concatenate to form y[7:0].
- Use a single internal wire named Co_temp to connect the nibbles.

4-bit block:
- Name: dut_dependency_3
- Ports: input a[3:0], b[3:0], Cin; output y[3:0], Co.
- Must instantiate exactly two dut_dependency_4 blocks with a single internal wire named Co_temp connecting lower to upper bits similarly.

2-bit block:
- Name: dut_dependency_4
- Ports: input a[1:0], b[1:0], Cin; output y[1:0], Co.
- Must instantiate exactly two dut_dependency_5 blocks with a single internal wire named Co_temp connecting bit 0 to bit 1.

1-bit cell:

question_text:
Design a purely combinational 8-bit ripple-carry adder using a required 1-bit full-adder cell.

Top module:
- Name: dut
- Ports:
  - input [7:0] a
  - input [7:0] b
  - input cin
  - output [7:0] sum
  - output cout

You must build dut by chaining exactly eight instances of a 1-bit full-adder submodule named dut_dependency_2 with the interface:
- input a, input b, input cin, output sum, output cout

Behavior:
- Treat a[0] and b[0] as the least significant bits (LSB).
- For bit i = 0..7, the i-th full-adder computes sum[i] and a carry-out from inputs a[i], b[i], and the carry-in to that stage.
- The carry-in to bit 0 is the top-level cin.
- For i > 0, the carry-in to bit i is the carry-out of bit i−1.
- The top-level cout must be exactly the carry-out produced by the bit-7 (MSB) stage.

Equivalently, sum must equal the lower 8 bits of the unsigned addition a + b + cin, and cout must equal the carry-out of that addition (the ninth bit).

Timing/semantics:
- No clock or reset; outputs must reflect input changes combinationally (no latches/flip-flops).
- No tri-states; assume inputs are 0/1 values.

Example cases:
- a=8'h00, b=8'h00, cin=1'b1 → sum=8'h01, cout=1'b0
- a=8'hFF, b=8'h00, cin=1'b1 → sum=8'h00, cout=1'b1
- a=8'hAA, b=8'h55, cin=1'b0 → sum=8'hFF, cout=1'b0

Implement both dut and the required dut_dependency_2 submodule as described.

question_text:
Design a combinational 8-bit adder module named dut with the following interface:
- Inputs: a[7:0], b[7:0] (unsigned, where bit 0 is the least significant bit), cin (1-bit carry-in).
- Outputs: sum[7:0], cout (1-bit carry-out).

Functional requirement:
Compute the unsigned binary addition of a + b + cin. The output sum must be the least significant 8 bits of the result, and cout must be the carry-out produced by the most significant bit (bit 7) addition. For all input combinations, outputs must be purely combinational (no clocks, latches, or sequential elements) and settle to deterministic 0/1 values (no X/Z).

Structural requirement:
You are provided a 1-bit full-adder primitive dut_dependency_2 with ports (a, b, cin, sum, cout), each 1 bit wide, whose combinational behavior is equivalent to {cout, sum} = a + b + cin. Build the 8-bit adder by instantiating exactly eight copies of dut_dependency_2. For bit i = 0..7, connect a[i], b[i], and a carry-in to produce sum[i] and a carry-out; the carry-out of bit i must feed the carry-in of bit i+1. Use cin as the carry-in for bit 0. The carry-out of bit 7 must drive the top-level cout.

Timing/edge conditions:
- No clock or reset signals are used.
- Behavior is purely level-sensitive: outputs reflect the current inputs after combinational propagation.

Your submission must adhere strictly to the specified interface and structural constraints.

question_text:
Design a purely combinational 8-bit ripple-carry adder using a provided 1-bit full-adder primitive.

Top-level module:
- Name: dut
- Inputs:
  - a[7:0]: 8-bit addend (bit 0 is LSB, bit 7 is MSB)
  - b[7:0]: 8-bit addend (bit 0 is LSB, bit 7 is MSB)
  - cin: 1-bit carry-in to the LSB stage
- Outputs:
  - sum[7:0]: 8-bit sum (bit 0 is LSB)
  - cout: 1-bit carry-out from the MSB stage

A helper module dut_dependency_2 is available and must be used as the only arithmetic primitive:
- Interface: input a, input b, input cin, output sum, output cout
- Behavior: 1-bit full adder; its outputs are combinationally equivalent to {cout, sum} = a + b + cin.

Requirements:
- Instantiate dut_dependency_2 exactly eight times, one per bit position i = 0..7.
- For bit i, connect a[i] and b[i] to the instance’s a and b.
- The LSB stage (i=0) must use the top-level cin as its carry-in.
- For each stage i (0..6), the instance’s carry-out must feed the next stage’s carry-in (i+1).
- The MSB stage (i=7) produces the final carry-out that must drive the top-level cout.
- Implement the carry chain using a single internal vector named c declared wide enough to hold carries for all stages; expose the stage i carry-out on c[i], and drive the top-level cout solely from c[7].
- No clocks, resets, or sequential logic; no arithmetic operators (+, -, etc.) outside the provided dut_dependency_2.

The design must be fully combinational and reflect a standard LSB-to-MSB ripple-carry topology as specified.

question_text:
Design a purely combinational 8-bit ripple-carry adder using a required 1-bit full-adder primitive.

Top module:
- Name: dut
- Ports:
  - input [7:0] a
  - input [7:0] b
  - input cin
  - output [7:0] sum
  - output cout

Functional behavior:
- Treat a and b as unsigned. Compute the 9-bit result R = a + b + cin.
- sum must equal R[7:0].
- cout must equal R[8].
- Outputs update combinationally with zero-cycle latency; no clocks or resets.

Implementation constraints (to be strictly followed):
- Instantiate exactly eight instances of a 1-bit full adder module named dut_dependency_2, with ports (input a, input b, input cin, output sum, output cout).
- Instance names must be FA0, FA1, FA2, FA3, FA4, FA5, FA6, FA7.
- Use bitwise ripple from LSB to MSB:
  - FA0: connects to a[0], b[0], cin.
  - For i in 1..7: FAi connects to a[i], b[i], and the carry-out of FA(i−1).
- Declare an internal wire vector named c of width 9. Connect carries such that FAi.cout drives c[i], FAi.cin is c[i−1] (with FA0.cin driven by top-level cin), and assign top-level cout = c[7].
- Do not use generate/for statements; instantiate explicitly.

Verification hook (must be present but inert):
- Declare wire [8:0] expected_sum_check = a + b + cin.
- Include an always @(*) block guarded by a constant-false condition so it never triggers; inside, if ({cout, sum} !== expected_sum_check) then $display with the exact message "Sum mismatch detected" and call $stop.

Also implement dut_dependency_2 as a combinational 1-bit full adder: sum and cout are the two least-significant bits of (a + b + cin).

question_text:
Design a combinational 8-bit ripple-carry adder using a provided 1-bit full adder cell.

Module to implement:
- Name: dut
- Ports:
  - input [7:0] a
  - input [7:0] b
  - input cin
  - output [7:0] sum
  - output cout

Behavior:
- Treat a and b as unsigned 8-bit values and cin as a single-bit carry-in.
- Compute the 9-bit unsigned result of a + b + cin.
- Drive sum with the least-significant 8 bits of this result.
- Drive cout with the carry-out from the most significant bit stage (i.e., the ninth bit of the addition).
- The design must be purely combinational: outputs must reflect inputs without clocking, latching, or storage, and without any latency.

Structural requirement:
- You are provided a 1-bit full adder primitive named dut_dependency_2 with the following scalar ports: input a, input b, input cin, output sum, output cout. It performs a + b + cin for one bit.
- You must instantiate dut_dependency_2 exactly eight times, one per bit position i = 0..7.
  - Connect the LSB stage’s cin to the top-level cin.
  - Cascade each stage’s cout to the next stage’s cin (ripple carry from bit i to bit i+1).
  - Connect each stage’s sum to sum[i].
  - Connect the top-level cout to the MSB stage’s cout.
- Do not infer or use any other arithmetic (e.g., + on vectors), reduction operators, or sequential logic in the top-level module.

Assume no undefined timing or edge conditions; all behavior is defined for stable inputs only.

Design a purely combinational 8-bit adder ring using a provided 1-bit full-adder submodule.

Top-level module:
- Name: dut
- Inputs:
  - a[7:0], b[7:0] (bit 0 is LSB)
  - cin (1 bit, intentionally unused)
- Outputs:
  - sum[7:0] (bit 0 is LSB)
  - cout (1 bit)

Submodule provided to you:
- Name: dut_dependency_2
- Ports: input a, input b, input cin, output sum, output cout
- Behavior: one-bit full adder such that the 2-bit value {cout, sum} equals a + b + cin.

Requirements:
- Instantiate exactly eight dut_dependency_2 stages, one per bit index i = 0..7, using:
  - stage i inputs: a[i], b[i], and a carry-in defined below
  - stage i outputs: sum[i] and an internal carry-out for that stage
- Ripple the carry-out forward by index: the carry-in of stage i (for i = 1..7) must be the carry-out of stage i−1.
- Wrap-around carry: the carry-in of stage 0 must be the carry-out of stage 7.
- Drive the top-level cout with the carry-out of stage 7.
- The top-level cin input must not influence any internal connection or output (it is intentionally unused).
- No clocks, resets, latches, or sequential logic; implement as combinational wiring only. No additional logic outside the eight specified submodule instances.

The implementation must conform exactly to this interconnection and produce sum and cout consistent with the described circular ripple-carry network.

question_text:
Design a purely combinational 8-bit adder with a circular carry chain.

Top-level module:
- Name: dut
- Ports:
  - input [7:0] a
  - input [7:0] b
  - input cin (present but must be ignored; do not connect it to any logic)
  - output [7:0] sum
  - output cout

You are provided a 1-bit full-adder primitive:
- Module name: dut_dependency_2
- Ports: input a, input b, input cin, output sum, output cout
- Behavior: {cout, sum} = a + b + cin (unsigned, 1-bit a/b/cin)

Requirements:
- Instantiate exactly eight dut_dependency_2 instances, one per bit, named FA0 through FA7.
- For bit i (0 to 7), connect a[i] and b[i] to the corresponding instance’s a and b.
- The carry chain is circular:
  - FA0’s cin is driven by the carry-out of FA7.
  - For i = 1..7, FAi’s cin is driven by the carry-out of FA(i−1).
- sum[i] is driven by the sum output of FAi.
- The top-level cout must be driven by the carry-out of FA7.
- Do not derive sum or cout from any arithmetic other than through the dut_dependency_2 instances. Do not use always blocks, generates, or additional modules.
- No other logic may use cin; it is a dummy input and must not affect any output.

The resulting design must implement the unique circular-ripple relation where each bit’s carry-in is the previous bit’s carry-out, with bit 0’s carry-in equal to bit 7’s carry-out, and cout equals the carry-out of bit 7.

question_text:
Design a purely combinational 8-bit ripple-carry adder built from 1-bit full adders.

Interface:
- Top-level module name: dut
  - Inputs: a[7:0], b[7:0] (unsigned), cin (1-bit)
  - Outputs: sum[7:0] (unsigned), cout (1-bit)
- Child module name: dut_dependency_2
  - Inputs: a, b, cin (all 1-bit)
  - Outputs: sum, cout (both 1-bit)

Functional requirements:
- dut_dependency_2 must implement a 1-bit full adder: for any change on a, b, or cin, drive outputs so that {cout, sum} equals the 2-bit unsigned result of a + b + cin.
- dut must compute the unsigned 9-bit sum S = a + b + cin and drive:
  - sum = S[7:0]
  - cout = S[8]
- Construct dut strictly by instantiating exactly eight dut_dependency_2 blocks named FA0, FA1, …, FA7, forming a ripple-carry chain:
  - For bit index i (0 is LSB, 7 is MSB), FAi adds a[i], b[i], and a carry-in.
  - FA0’s carry-in is the top-level cin.
  - For i = 0..6, the carry-out of FAi is the carry-in of FA(i+1).
  - The top-level cout is the carry-out produced by FA7 (the MSB stage).
  - sum[i] is driven by the sum output of FAi.

Timing/other constraints:
- No clocks or resets; outputs must reflect input changes combinationally (no latches or sequential logic).
- Do not modify the specified ports or widths; do not add extra I/O.
- Aside from wiring/assignments needed to connect instances, do not insert additional arithmetic that changes the required behavior.

question_text:
Design a combinational 8-bit ripple adder with a nonstandard carry rule.

Interface:
- Module name: dut
- Inputs: a[7:0], b[7:0], cin (1-bit)
- Outputs: sum[7:0], cout (1-bit)

You must build the 8-bit adder by instantiating exactly eight identical 1-bit cells named dut_dependency_2, connected in a ripple chain from bit 0 (LSB) to bit 7 (MSB). Each dut_dependency_2 has the following ports:
- Inputs: a (1-bit), b (1-bit), cin (1-bit)
- Outputs: sum (1-bit), cout (1-bit)

Behavior (combinational, no clocks/resets):
- Let c0 = cin. For each bit i in 0..7, define:
  - xi = a[i] XOR b[i]
  - sum[i] = xi XOR ci
  - ci+1 = xi AND ci
- The carry-in to bit i is ci, and the dut_dependency_2 for that bit must output sum[i] and cout = ci+1.
- Connect the ripple so that the cout of bit i feeds the cin of bit i+1.
- The top-level output cout must be the cout produced by the bit-7 cell (i.e., c8).

Notes:
- This “different-only carry” adder never generates a carry from a[i] and b[i] alone; a carry propagates only when exactly one of a[i], b[i] is 1 and the incoming carry is 1.
- All logic is purely combinational; outputs must update immediately with inputs.
- Do not add or remove ports; adhere strictly to the specified interfaces and naming.

Your task is to implement dut and dut_dependency_2 to satisfy the above behavior exactly.

question_text:
Design a purely combinational Verilog module named dut that computes an “offset-corrected” nibble sum.

Interface:
- Inputs:
  - A[3:0], B[3:0]: unsigned 4-bit values (0–15).
  - Cin: 1-bit carry-in (0 or 1).
- Outputs:
  - Sum[3:0]: unsigned 4-bit result.
  - Cout: 1-bit flag.

Behavior:
- Let S be the 5-bit unsigned sum S = A + B + Cin.
- Set Cout = 1 if and only if S > 9; otherwise Cout = 0.
- Independently of Cout, produce Sum as the lower 4 bits of (S + 6), i.e., Sum = (S + 6) mod 16. Do not conditionally add 6; the +6 offset is always applied.
- No clock or reset is used. Outputs must reflect the current inputs combinationally with zero-cycle latency (no latches, flops, or state).
- All arithmetic is unsigned. Inputs are guaranteed to be 0/1 (no X/Z).

Examples (unsigned):
- A=4'b0100 (4), B=4'b0011 (3), Cin=1'b1 ⇒ S=8, Cout=0, Sum=(8+6)=14 ⇒ Sum=4'b1110.
- A=4'b1001 (9), B=4'b1001 (9), Cin=1'b1 ⇒ S=19, Cout=1, Sum=(19+6)=25 mod16=9 ⇒ Sum=4'b1001.
- A=4'b0000 (0), B=4'b0000 (0), Cin=1'b0 ⇒ S=0, Cout=0, Sum=(0+6)=6 ⇒ Sum=4'b0110.

Implement only the described combinational logic with the exact port names and widths.

Design a combinational Verilog module named dut that implements a biased 4-bit adder with a threshold carry-out. The interface is:
- Inputs: A[3:0], B[3:0] (unsigned 4-bit), Cin (unsigned 1-bit)
- Outputs: Sum[3:0] (unsigned 4-bit), Cout (unsigned 1-bit)

Behavior:
1) Compute an intermediate unsigned 5-bit sum S = A + B + Cin.
2) Set Cout = 1 if S > 9, else Cout = 0.
3) Independently of Cout and regardless of the value of S, form Sum by taking the least significant 4 bits of (S + 6). That is, Sum = (S + 6) mod 16.

Additional notes:
- All arithmetic is unsigned.
- There is no clock or reset; the logic must be purely combinational with no state.
- A and B may be any 4-bit values (0–15). No special-casing is required for invalid BCD digits; always apply the rules above.
- No undefined or don’t-care outputs; produce a deterministic result for all input combinations.

Examples (A, B, Cin -> Sum, Cout):
- 3, 1, 0: S = 4 → Cout = 0; Sum = (4 + 6) mod 16 = 10 (1010).
- 7, 5, 0: S = 12 → Cout = 1; Sum = (12 + 6) mod 16 = 2 (0010).
- 15, 15, 1: S = 31 → Cout = 1; Sum = (31 + 6) mod 16 = 5 (0101).

Implement dut to exactly match this behavior and interface.

Design a combinational module named dut that implements a corrected-nibble adder with a fixed offset and a threshold flag.

Interface:
- Inputs:
  - A[3:0], B[3:0]: unsigned 4-bit operands
  - Cin: unsigned 1-bit carry-in
- Outputs:
  - Sum[3:0]: unsigned 4-bit result
  - Cout: unsigned 1-bit flag

Behavior:
1) Form a 5-bit unsigned intermediate sum s = A + B + Cin.
2) Set Cout = 1 if and only if s > 9 (decimal); otherwise Cout = 0. This comparison uses s exactly as computed in step 1.
3) Compute Sum as the least significant 4 bits of (s + 6). The constant 6 (binary 0110) is always added to s for Sum, regardless of the value of Cout. Any bits above bit 3 in (s + 6) are discarded. No other corrections or conditional additions are performed.

Timing:
- Purely combinational: outputs must reflect the current inputs within the same cycle. No clock, reset, or handshaking.

Arithmetic and constraints:
- All arithmetic is unsigned.
- Inputs A and B may be any 4-bit values (0–15); behavior must follow the rules above for all combinations.
- Sum wraps modulo 16 by construction (low 4 bits of s + 6).

Examples (decimal shown with binary notes):
- A=3, B=5, Cin=0: s=8 → Cout=0; s+6=14 → Sum=1110 (14).
- A=9, B=9, Cin=1: s=19 → Cout=1; s+6=25 → Sum=1001 (9).
- A=4, B=6, Cin=1: s=11 → Cout=1; s+6=17 → Sum=0001 (1).

Implement exactly this behavior and interface.

Design a purely combinational module dut that performs a “truncated decimal adjust” on the 4-bit sum of two 4-bit inputs and a carry-in.

Interface:
- Inputs: A[3:0], B[3:0], Cin (1-bit)
- Outputs: Sum[3:0], Cout (1-bit)

Design a combinational module dut with the following interface:
- input [7:0] in (bit 7 is MSB),
- input [2:0] ctrl,
- output [7:0] out.

Behavior:
The module implements a staged logical right-barrel shift on in. Each ctrl bit enables an independent zero-fill right shift:
- If ctrl[2] = 1, first shift right by 4; else pass through.
- If ctrl[1] = 1, then shift the current value right by 2; else pass through.
- If ctrl[0] = 1, finally shift the current value right by 1; else pass through.

Vacated MSBs are filled with 0 at each enabled stage. Let s = 4*ctrl[2] + 2*ctrl[1] + 1*ctrl[0]. For all bit indices i where the output is defined (see exceptions below), out[i] must equal:
- out[i] = in[i + s] when i + s ≤ 7,
- out[i] = 0 when i + s > 7.

Exception (intentional don’t-care):
The bit position index 5 immediately after the optional 2-bit stage is unspecified. As a result:
- If ctrl[0] = 0, out[5] is don’t-care (may be 0 or 1 and will not be tested).
- If ctrl[0] = 1, out[4] is don’t-care (may be 0 or 1 and will not be tested).

All other output bits must strictly follow the defined logical right shift by s as above. The design is purely combinational (no clocks, latches, or state) and must react to input changes without latency.

  X[2] = in[6]
  X[1] = in[5]
  X[0] = in[4]

  Y[2] = X[4]

  out[4] = Y[5]

  out[2] = Y[3]
  out[1] = Y[2]
  out[0] = Y[1]

- ctrl[2] gates x
- ctrl[1] gates y
- ctrl[0] gates out

- y loads from x:

Design a combinationally connected, level-sensitive, multi-stage bit router with latching behavior. Implement a module with:
- Inputs: in[7:0], ctrl[2:0]
- Output: out[7:0]

The data path consists of three cascaded banks of transparent latches, each enabled by one control bit. There is no clock and no reset. All latches are level-sensitive:
- When a stage’s enable is 1, that stage becomes transparent and immediately drives its outputs from the specified inputs below.
- When its enable is 0, that stage holds its previously latched values (initial values are undefined; tests will not rely on power-up state).

Define the three stages conceptually as vectors A[7:0], B[7:0], and the final output out[7:0]:

Stage A (enabled by ctrl[2]): when ctrl[2]=1,
- A[7]=0, A[6]=0, A[5]=0, A[4]=0,
- A[3]=in[7], A[2]=in[6], A[1]=in[5], A[0]=in[4];
else A holds its previous values.

Stage B (enabled by ctrl[1]): when ctrl[1]=1,
- B[7]=0, B[6]=0,
- B[5]=A[7], B[4]=A[6], B[3]=A[5], B[2]=A[4], B[1]=A[3], B[0]=A[2];
else B holds its previous values.

Stage C (enabled by ctrl[0]): when ctrl[0]=1,
- out[7]=B[7], out[6]=B[7], out[5]=B[6], out[4]=B[5],
- out[3]=B[4], out[2]=B[3], out[1]=B[2], out[0]=B[1];
else out holds its previous values.

All stages are independent and may be enabled in any combination; if multiple enables are 1 simultaneously, transparency composes through the cascade in the same cycle. Your solution must strictly implement this level-sensitive, hold-when-disabled behavior and exact bit mapping.

question_text:
Design a purely combinational Verilog module with the following interface:
- input [7:0] in
- input [2:0] ctrl (bit fields: ctrl[2]=c2, ctrl[1]=c1, ctrl[0]=c0)
- output [7:0] out

The output is produced by three cascaded combinational stages. Define temporary 8-bit vectors A and B as follows:

Stage A (c2-controlled preprocessing):
- If c2 = 0: A = in.
- If c2 = 1: A[7:4] = 4'b0000 and A[3:0] = {in[7], in[6], in[5], in[4]}.

Stage B (mix/shift with c1; note the special rule for bit 5):
- B[7] = (c1 ? 1'b0 : A[7])
- B[6] = (c1 ? 1'b0 : A[6])
- B[5] = (c2 ? A[7] : A[5])  // independent of c1
- B[4] = (c1 ? A[6] : A[4])
- B[3] = (c1 ? A[5] : A[3])
- B[2] = (c1 ? A[4] : A[2])
- B[1] = (c1 ? A[3] : A[1])
- B[0] = (c1 ? A[2] : A[0])

Stage C (c0-controlled final alignment):
- out[7] = (c0 ? 1'b0 : B[7])
- out[6] = (c0 ? B[7] : B[6])
- out[5] = (c0 ? B[6] : B[5])
- out[4] = (c0 ? B[5] : B[4])
- out[3] = (c0 ? B[4] : B[3])
- out[2] = (c0 ? B[3] : B[2])
- out[1] = (c0 ? B[2] : B[1])
- out[0] = (c0 ? B[1] : B[0])

Requirements:
- No clock or reset; out must reflect in and ctrl changes combinationally.
- Do not infer latches or use undefined/X/Z behavior.
- Implement exactly the bit-wise behavior above.

question_text:
Design a synchronous 24-hour timekeeper with three counters: seconds, minutes, and hours.

Interface:
- Inputs:
  - CLK: system clock.
  - RST: reserved input; must be ignored (no reset behavior).
- Outputs:
  - Secs[5:0], Mins[5:0], Hours[5:0].

Behavior (all updates occur on the rising edge of CLK and are computed from the values present immediately before that edge):
- Secs counts 0 to 59, then wraps to 0. Specifically, on each rising edge:
  - If Secs was 59, Secs becomes 0.
  - Otherwise, Secs increments by 1.
- Mins changes only when Secs was 59:
  - If Mins was 59 and Secs was 59, Mins becomes 0.
  - Else if Secs was 59, Mins increments by 1.
  - Otherwise, Mins holds its value.
- Hours changes only when both Mins and Secs were 59:
  - If Hours was 23 and both Mins and Secs were 59, Hours becomes 0.
  - Else if both Mins and Secs were 59, Hours increments by 1.
  - Otherwise, Hours holds its value.

Ranges:
- Secs and Mins must be within 0–59.
- Hours must be within 0–23.

There is no enable, load, or reset effect; RST must be ignored. Initial values of Hours/Mins/Secs are unspecified and will not be directly tested; only the synchronous next-state behavior described above will be verified (e.g., 23:59:59 transitions to 00:00:00 on the next CLK rising edge).

Design a synchronous 24-hour timekeeper with cascading counters. Implement module dut with the following interface:
- Inputs: CLK (clock), RST (unused; see below).
- Outputs: Hours[5:0], Mins[5:0], Secs[5:0] (all unsigned, registered).

Behavior:
- All state updates occur only on the rising edge of CLK. Between edges, outputs must remain stable.
- RST is a reserved input that must not affect the behavior; it may be driven arbitrarily and must be ignored by the design.
- At each rising edge, evaluate transitions using the values present at that edge before any updates (i.e., all comparisons are against the “old” values sampled at the same clock edge):
  - Seconds (Secs): if Secs == 59, set Secs to 0; otherwise, increment Secs by 1.
  - Minutes (Mins): if Secs == 59 and Mins == 59, set Mins to 0; else if Secs == 59, increment Mins by 1; otherwise, hold Mins.
  - Hours (Hours): if Secs == 59 and Mins == 59 and Hours == 23, set Hours to 0; else if Secs == 59 and Mins == 59, increment Hours by 1; otherwise, hold Hours.
- No other wrap-around or clamping is permitted beyond the rules above.
- Initial values of Hours, Mins, and Secs are unspecified and will not be tested; only the defined transitions across clock edges will be verified.

Your solution must exactly follow these synchronous update rules and ignore RST under all circumstances.

Design a synchronous digital clock counter module named dut with the following interface:
- Inputs:
  - CLK: clock
  - RST: reserved input; must have no effect on behavior
- Outputs (6-bit each): Hours, Mins, Secs

1) Seconds:
   - If Secs equals 59 at a rising edge, set Secs to 0.
   - Otherwise, increment Secs by 1.
2) Minutes:
   - Minutes update only on edges where Secs equals 59 (as observed at that same edge).
   - If Mins equals 59 and Secs equals 59 at a rising edge, set Mins to 0.
   - Else if Secs equals 59 at a rising edge, increment Mins by 1.
   - Otherwise, hold Mins.

   - Hours update only on edges where both Mins equals 59 and Secs equals 59 (as observed at that same edge).

   - Else if Mins equals 59 and Secs equals 59 at a rising edge, increment Hours by 1.
