- No asynchronous or synchronous reset behavior; do not initialize outputs. RST is a no-op under all conditions.

Design a synchronous timekeeper in Verilog.

Module name and interface:
- module dut(input CLK, input RST, output [5:0] Hours, output [5:0] Mins, output [5:0] Secs);

Behavior:
- All outputs are 6-bit unsigned registers that only change on the rising edge of CLK.
- RST is a reserved input and must be ignored; asserting or deasserting RST has no effect on any output.
- On each rising edge of CLK, compute next values from the values present immediately before that edge (i.e., decisions use the pre-edge Hours/Mins/Secs):
  - Secs next:
    - If Secs == 59, next Secs = 0.
    - Else, next Secs = Secs + 1.
  - Mins next:
    - If (Mins == 59) and (Secs == 59), next Mins = 0.
    - Else if (Secs == 59), next Mins = Mins + 1.
    - Else, next Mins = Mins (hold).
  - Hours next:
    - If (Hours == 23) and (Mins == 59) and (Secs == 59), next Hours = 0.
    - Else if (Mins == 59) and (Secs == 59), next Hours = Hours + 1.
    - Else, next Hours = Hours (hold).
- This yields the cascade: Secs counts 0..59, Mins increments only when Secs equals 59, Hours increments only when both Mins and Secs equal their terminal values; at 23:59:59 the next state is 00:00:00.

Notes:
- Do not assume any initial values; the grader will observe step-to-step transitions only.
- No combinational outputs; only registered updates on CLK rising edges are allowed.

- output [5:0] Secs

- Asynchronous reset: On the rising edge of RST, perform this conditional clear based on the values at that instant:
  - If Mins == 59 and Secs == 59, do not change Hours, Mins, or Secs (reset has no effect).
  - Otherwise, set Hours = 0, Mins = 0, Secs = 0.
- Synchronous counting (evaluated on each rising edge of CLK while RST is low, using the values present just before the edge):
  - Seconds:
    - If Secs == 59, set Secs to 0; else increment Secs by 1.
  - Minutes:
    - If Mins == 59 and Secs == 59, set Mins to 0.
    - Else if Secs == 59, increment Mins by 1.
    - Else hold Mins.
  - Hours (24-hour cycle):
    - If Hours == 23 and Mins == 59 and Secs == 59, set Hours to 0.
    - Else if Mins == 59 and Secs == 59, increment Hours by 1.
    - Else hold Hours.

- Secs increments by 1 each cycle; when Secs was 59 on that edge, it becomes 0.
- Mins holds unless Secs was 59 on that edge; then Mins increments by 1. If both Mins was 59 and Secs was 59 on that edge, Mins becomes 0.
- Hours holds unless both Mins and Secs were 59 on that edge; then Hours increments by 1. If Hours was 23 and both Mins and Secs were 59 on that edge, Hours becomes 0.

module dut
(
  input clk,
  input rst_n,
  output reg clk_div
);

  reg [4:0] r;

  always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
    if(!rst_n) begin
      r <= 5'b0;
    end else begin
      if(r == 5'd19) begin
        r <= 5'b0;
      end else begin
        r <= r + 1'b1;
      end
    end
  end


  always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
    if(!rst_n) begin
      clk_div <= 1'b0;
    end else begin
      if((r == 5'd0) || (r == 5'd11)) begin
        clk_div <= 1'b1;
      end else begin
        clk_div <= 1'b0;
      end
    end
  end


  always @(negedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
    if(!rst_n) begin
      clk_div <= 1'b0;
    end else begin
      if((r == 5'd1) || (r == 5'd11)) begin
        clk_div <= 1'b1;
      end else begin
        clk_div <= 1'b0;
      end
    end
  end


endmodule

Design a synthesizable RTL module named dut with the following interface and behavior:

  - input rst_n: active-low, asynchronous reset.
  - input clk: free-running clock.

- Parameters:
  - MUL2_DIV_CLK: positive integer, default value 7.

- Internal state:
  - A 4-bit register cnt that:
    - Asynchronously clears to 0 when rst_n is 0.
    - On each rising edge of clk when rst_n is 1, increments by 1.
    - When cnt equals MUL2_DIV_CLK − 1 on a rising edge, the next value must wrap to 0 (i.e., modulo MUL2_DIV_CLK behavior).
    - This counter is reserved for future use and must not affect any outputs.

- Clock-domain registers:
  - A 1-bit register clk_ave_r that:
    - Asynchronously clears to 0 when rst_n is 0.
    - On each rising edge of clk when rst_n is 1, retains its previous value (no toggling or external drive).
  - A 1-bit register clk_adjust_r that:
    - Asynchronously clears to 0 when rst_n is 0.
    - On each falling edge of clk when rst_n is 1, retains its previous value (no toggling or external drive).

- Output definition:
  - clk_div must be the logical OR of clk_ave_r and clk_adjust_r.

Timing/edge conditions:
- Use edge-triggered flip-flops with sensitivity to posedge clk or negedge clk, and negedge rst_n for asynchronous reset.
- No combinational or sequential logic may modify clk_ave_r or clk_adjust_r other than their defined self-retention and reset.
- No latches or additional outputs are allowed.

The observable behavior is that, after reset deassertion, clk_div remains 0 at all times regardless of clk or cnt.

4) Reset dominance:

Design a synthesizable RTL module named dut that generates a divided clock with near-50% duty cycle using both clock edges.

Interface:
- Inputs: clk (free-running clock), rst_n (asynchronous active-low reset).
- Output: clk_div (1-bit).

Parameters:
- NUM_DIV is an integer parameter with default value 5. Assume NUM_DIV is an odd integer greater than 1.

Behavior:
- While rst_n is 0, the design must immediately and asynchronously force clk_div = 1.
- Define a modulo-NUM_DIV counter c that advances by +1 on every rising edge of clk and wraps to 0 after NUM_DIV − 1. After reset is released, c must start from 0.
- Let TH = floor(NUM_DIV/2). The output must be generated from the same counter value c sampled on both edges as follows:
  - On each rising edge of clk, compute P = 1 if c_before < TH, else 0. Register P on that rising edge.
  - On each falling edge of clk, compute F = 1 if current c (after the most recent rising-edge update) < TH, else 0. Register F on that falling edge.
  - The output clk_div must be the logical OR of the registered P and F.
- clk_div may only change at clock edges; it must be glitch-free between edges.
- Upon reset deassertion, the first observable clk_div value must be 1 until the above rules cause a change.

Do not add or remove ports. The design must satisfy the exact timing and edge-sampling behavior described above for all odd NUM_DIV ≥ 3 (default 5).

Design a synthesizable Verilog module named dut that generates a divided clock with a precise odd-ratio waveform using both edges of the input clock.

Interface:
- input clk: free-running clock.
- input rst_n: asynchronous, active-low reset.
- output clk_div: divided clock output.

Behavioral requirements:
- When rst_n = 0, clk_div must be immediately and continuously forced to 1, regardless of clk.
- When rst_n transitions to 1, the output phase is reinitialized. Starting at the first rising edge of clk that occurs after rst_n = 1, consider consecutive half-cycles of clk (each half-cycle spans between successive edges: rising→falling→rising→…).
- Over these half-cycles, clk_div must follow this exact repeating pattern:
  H, H, H, H, L, L, L, L, L, H, (then repeat from the beginning)
  where H = logic 1 and L = logic 0.
- The output may change only at edges of clk (never between edges). The first H→L transition occurs on a rising edge; the first L→H transition occurs on a falling edge, consistent with the pattern above.
- The resulting clk_div has a period of 10 half-cycles (5 full clk periods), i.e., a divide-by-5 of clk, with an average duty cycle of exactly 50% over each 5-cycle period.

Notes:
- No additional ports or handshakes are allowed.
- The design must be glitch-free per the edge-change rule above and must adhere exactly to the specified sequence after every deassertion of rst_n.

Design a Verilog RTL module named dut with the following interface:
- Inputs: IN (1-bit serial data), CLK (clock), RST (asynchronous active-high reset)
- Output: MATCH (1-bit)

Behavior:
- IN is sampled on each rising edge of CLK.
- When RST is 1, the detector must immediately (asynchronously) return to its initial state and drive MATCH = 0, regardless of CLK.
- Detect the bit pattern 10011 in the serial stream with overlap allowed. The pattern is considered detected on the same rising edge of CLK that samples the final ‘1’ of 10011.
- MATCH must assert to 1 precisely when that final ‘1’ is sampled (i.e., in the same cycle as detection). After it becomes 1, MATCH must remain 1 until RST is asserted; no other condition may clear it.
- On cycles where RST = 0 and no new detection occurs, MATCH must retain its previous value (do not force it low between detections).
- The detector must correctly handle overlapping occurrences (e.g., the stream 100110011 should register detection on the 5th and 10th sampled bits).

Timing/edge requirements:
- State updates occur on the rising edge of CLK.
- RST is asynchronous and active-high; when asserted, both the internal state and MATCH must reflect reset immediately.

Implement only the specified I/O and behavior. Any deviation that fails to assert MATCH exactly on detection, hold MATCH high thereafter, support overlap, or asynchronously clear on RST should be considered incorrect.

Design a synchronous serial pattern detector with a sticky match flag.

Interface:
- module name: dut
- inputs: IN (1-bit data), CLK (clock), RST (asynchronous active-high reset)
- output: MATCH (1-bit)

Timing and reset:
- IN is sampled on each rising edge of CLK.
- On the rising edge of RST, the detector returns to its initial state. While RST=1, MATCH must be 0.
- After RST is deasserted, operation resumes on subsequent CLK edges.

Behavior:
- Detect the bit pattern P = 1 0 0 1 1 in the input stream with overlap allowed.
- Let k denote the length (0–5) of the longest prefix of P that is a suffix of all bits received up to the previous cycle. On each rising edge of CLK, update k according to:
  - k=0: IN=1 → k=1; IN=0 → k=0
  - k=1: IN=0 → k=2; IN=1 → k=1
  - k=2: IN=0 → k=3; IN=1 → k=1
  - k=3: IN=1 → k=4; IN=0 → k=0
  - k=4: IN=1 → k=5; IN=0 → k=2
  - k=5: IN=1 → k=1; IN=0 → k=2
- MATCH is a sticky flag: it is asserted to 1 exactly on the CLK cycle when IN=1 and the previous k=4 (i.e., when P is first completed), and it must remain 1 thereafter until RST is asserted. MATCH must not deassert due to further inputs.

Initial conditions:
- After reset (before any valid CLK edge with RST=0), k=0 and MATCH=0.

Implement dut to satisfy the above behavior precisely.

Design a finite-state pattern detector with a sticky match output.

Module interface:
- module dut(IN, MATCH, CLK, RST);
- IN: 1-bit serial data input.
- CLK: clock.
- RST: asynchronous, active-high reset.
- MATCH: 1-bit output.

Behavior:
- The detector scans IN on rising edges of CLK for the sequence 1,0,0,1,1 (i.e., “10011”), allowing overlaps.
- MATCH must assert (become 1) in the same clock cycle that the fifth bit of this sequence (the final ‘1’) is presented on IN. This means MATCH is a Mealy-style output dependent on the current internal state and the current IN value; it must not wait for a subsequent clock edge to assert.
- Once MATCH has asserted at least once, it must remain 1 (sticky) until RST is asserted. MATCH must never deassert due to further inputs or clocks; only RST may clear it.
- While RST is high, the detector is in its idle state and MATCH must be 0 regardless of IN or CLK. On a rising edge of RST, the internal state resets immediately; after RST returns low, scanning resumes from idle on the next rising CLK.
- Overlaps are required: after recognizing “10011”, the detector must continue tracking so that sequences like “...100110011...” cause MATCH to assert when the 5th and 10th bits of those subsequences arrive.

Constraints:
- Use only the specified ports; no additional I/O.
- IN is considered stable around each rising edge of CLK for sampling purposes.

Implement dut to meet these exact timing and behavioral requirements.

Design a synchronous RTL module that accumulates 16×16-bit unsigned products using a level-sensitive start signal and a one-cycle done pulse.

Interface:
- clk: system clock (positive edge).
- rst_n: asynchronous, active-low reset.
- start: level input; holds the operation active while high.
- ain, bin: 16-bit unsigned operands.
- yout: 32-bit unsigned accumulator output.
- done: status output.

Behavior:
- Reset: When rst_n=0, the module is idle; areg, breg are cleared to 0, done=0. Assume start=0 during reset; yout must be 0 in this condition.
- Arming and latching: When rst_n=1 and the module is idle (armed) with start=1 on a rising clk edge, latch ain and bin into internal registers.
- Processing: While start remains 1, perform exactly 16 sequential cycles, j=0..15 (LSB to MSB of the latched ain). On cycle j+1, if bit j of the latched ain is 1, add (bin zero-extended to 32 bits) left-shifted by j to yout; otherwise leave yout unchanged. yout changes only on these conditional-add cycles.
- Completion: Concurrent with processing bit 15 (the 16th cycle), assert done=1 for exactly one clock cycle. On the next clock, deassert done to 0 and perform no further updates while start remains 1.
- Re-arming: While start=0 on any rising clk edge, the module is idle: the internal cycle counter is 0, areg/breg/yout hold their values, done=0. A subsequent start=1 begins a new 16-cycle operation by latching ain/bin as above.
- Operand stability: Changes on ain/bin during processing have no effect; only the latched values are used.
- Accumulation: yout is not cleared between operations except by reset; each operation adds its product to the existing yout.

Timing and outputs must strictly follow the above.

Design a sequential unsigned multiplier with the following I/O:
- clk: clock
- rst_n: active-low asynchronous reset
- start: level-sensitive run enable
- ain[15:0], bin[15:0]: 16-bit unsigned inputs
- yout[31:0]: 32-bit unsigned output
- done: status output

Behavior:
- When rst_n=0, immediately clear all internal state: yout=0, done=0, and the step index s=0. Operation resumes when rst_n returns high.
- Define a step index s in [0..17] that increments by 1 on each rising edge of clk only if start=1 and s<17; otherwise s holds its value (s saturates at 17 until the next reset).
- On the rising edge when start=1 and s==0, capture ain and bin into internal registers A and B. After this capture, changes on ain/bin must not affect the ongoing operation.
- For k=0..15, on the rising edge when s==k+1 (i.e., the (k+1)th qualified cycle with start=1):
  - If bit k of A is 1, update yout := yout + (zero-extended B) << k.
  - Otherwise, yout holds its previous value.
- yout must not be written in any other cycle. After s reaches 17, yout holds the final product A*B indefinitely until reset.
- done behavior: set done=1 precisely in cycles where s==16; set done=0 precisely in cycles where s==17; in all other cycles, retain its previous value. If start is deasserted before completion, s stalls and outputs behave per the above rules.

Assume no new operation starts without a reset. Timing is evaluated on clk rising edges; all widths and shifts are unsigned.

Design an RTL module dut with the following interface:
- Inputs: clk, rst_n (asynchronous active-low reset), start, ain[15:0], bin[15:0]
- Outputs: yout[31:0], done

Functionality:
- When rst_n is low, yout must be 0, done must be 0, and all internal state must reset.
- After reset is released, the module is idle until start=1. On the first clock edge with start=1 while idle, latch ain and bin into internal registers; all computation uses these latched values only.
- The multiplication is unsigned 16×16, computed iteratively over exactly 16 advancement cycles, one per bit of the latched ain (LSB first). The internal “advancement” occurs only on clock cycles where start=1; if start=0, the operation pauses (no advancement, outputs hold).
  - On advancement cycle k (k=1..16), examine bit k−1 of the latched ain; if it is 1, add (bin << (k−1)) to yout; otherwise yout is unchanged. yout updates only on clock edges and only during these advancement cycles.
- When the 16th advancement completes, assert done=1. done remains 1 until exactly one additional advancement cycle occurs (i.e., a subsequent clock with start=1), after which done deasserts to 0. After this deassertion, the module enters a terminal state: it must ignore start, perform no further updates, and require a reset to begin a new operation.
- At all times, ain/bin changes after the initial latching must not affect the ongoing computation. yout holds the final 32-bit product after completion and remains stable until the next reset.

All behavior is synchronous to the rising edge of clk, except for rst_n.

Design a sequential 16×16 unsigned multiplier with a start/stop handshake and a one-shot operation per reset.

Interface:
- clk: clock.
- rst_n: asynchronous active-low reset.
- start: qualifies progress (see below).
- ain[15:0], bin[15:0]: 16-bit unsigned inputs.
- yout[31:0]: 32-bit output.
- done: completion flag.

Behavior and timing (all state updates on the rising edge of clk; rst_n is asynchronous):
- On rst_n deassertion (low), clear an internal 5-bit step counter to 0, set yout to 0, and deassert done.
- Progress occurs only when start=1. While start=1 and the step counter is less than 17, increment the step counter by 1 each rising edge. While start=0, hold the step counter.
- At step 0 when start=1, latch ain and bin into internal registers A and B.
- For each step k = 1..16, if bit (k−1) of A is 1, add (B zero-extended to 32 bits) left-shifted by (k−1) to a 32-bit accumulator; otherwise leave the accumulator unchanged. The accumulator equals yout and is cleared only by rst_n (not by start).
- Assert done=1 during any cycle in which the step counter equals 16. Deassert done=1→0 during any cycle in which the step counter equals 17. In all other cycles, done is 0.
- After the counter reaches 17, it must not advance further until rst_n is asserted low; start has no effect in this state.

Notes:
- The design must tolerate pauses: if start is deasserted mid-computation, processing resumes from the same step when start returns high.

- Reset behavior: When rst_n is 0, S1, S2, and mul_out are immediately cleared to 0. When rst_n returns to 1, normal operation resumes on the next rising clock edge.

- Latency is exactly one clock cycle: for stable inputs at cycle t, mul_out at cycle t+1 reflects the above computation; after reset deassertion, the first nonzero mul_out can appear no earlier than the second rising edge due to clearing.

(
  input clk,
  input rst,
  input [31:0] a,
  input [31:0] b,
  output reg [31:0] c
);


  always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
    if(rst) begin

    end else begin
      c <= c + a + b;

Design a Verilog RTL module named dut that implements a 4-state Mealy finite state machine with the following interface:
- Inputs:
  - clk: clock
  - rst_n: active-low asynchronous reset
  - data_in: 1-bit input
- Output:
  - data_out: 1-bit output

Timing and reset requirements:
- On the falling edge of rst_n, the FSM state must asynchronously reset to S0 immediately.
- On each rising edge of clk while rst_n=1, the current state updates to the next state defined below.
- The next-state and output logic are purely combinational functions of the current state and data_in in the same cycle.
- While rst_n=0, data_out must be 0 regardless of clk and data_in.

States and transitions (next-state function):
- From S0: if data_in=0, go to S1; else stay in S0.
- From S1: go to S2 (regardless of data_in).
- From S2: if data_in=0, go to S3; else go to S0.
- From S3: if data_in=1, go to S2; else go to S1.

Output function (Mealy):
- data_out is 1 if and only if rst_n=1, the current state is S2, and data_in=0; otherwise data_out is 0.

Additional notes:
- The FSM must start in S0 after any active-low reset.
- The specification requires combinational next-state and output logic (no additional clocking of data_out).
- Implement only the described behavior; no extra outputs or inputs.

Design a finite-state detector with the following interface:
- module dut(input clk, input rst_n, input data_in, output reg data_out).
- clk: rising-edge clock.
- rst_n: asynchronous active-low reset.
- data_in: 1-bit input sampled on each rising edge of clk.
- data_out: 1-bit output.

Behavior:
- While rst_n is low, data_out must be held 0. On any falling edge of rst_n, the internal state must reset immediately to an idle state (no partial progress).
- The detector searches for the pattern “0 then 1 then 0” in the sampled data_in stream with these rules:
  - From idle, ignore 1s; upon sampling a 0, enter “seen 0” state and remain there while 0s continue.
  - From “seen 0,” upon sampling a 1, enter “seen 0 then 1.”
  - From “seen 0 then 1,” if the next sampled bit is 0, assert data_out = 1 during that same cycle (the cycle in which the 0 is sampled), then transition into a latched terminal state that ignores all future inputs and never produces another pulse until reset. If instead a 1 is sampled, cancel progress and return to idle with no output.
- Outside the single-cycle assertion described above, data_out must be 0.

Timing requirements:
- State updates occur only on rising edges of clk.
- data_out must reflect the current cycle’s sampled input and state (i.e., the pulse occurs in the cycle the third 0 is sampled, not a later cycle).

Example (sampled per rising edge, rst_n=1 throughout):
data_in: 1,1,0,0,1,0,1,0 → data_out: 0,0,0,0,0,1,0,0; thereafter stays 0 until reset.

- Multiple leading 0’s before the first 1 do not cause a pulse (still waiting for the first 1). After seeing the required 1, a 1 on the next cycle cancels progress and returns to idle.
- Immediately after asserting data_out for the 0 that completes the 0–1–0 pattern, the detector must enter a permanent locked state: it never asserts data_out again and it never leaves this state regardless of future data_in values. Only reset can release the lock.

Reset and timing:
- rst_n is asynchronous and dominant: while rst_n=0, data_out must be 0 at all times, and internal state is cleared so that upon deassertion (rst_n=1) the detector is in the idle condition without waiting for a clock.

Design a synchronous finite-state detector with a terminal latch.

Interface:
- module name: dut
- inputs: clk (clock), rst_n (active-low asynchronous reset), data_in (1-bit)
- output: data_out (1-bit)

Reset behavior:
- While rst_n = 0, the state is immediately reset to Idle and data_out must be 0 asynchronously (no clock required).
- On rst_n rising back to 1, operation resumes from Idle.

Operation (state transitions occur on the rising edge of clk; data_in is sampled on that edge):
- Idle: Wait for data_in = 0. If data_in = 0 at a rising edge, transition to Seen0. Otherwise remain in Idle.
- Seen0: If data_in = 1 at a rising edge, transition to Armed. If data_in = 0, remain in Seen0.
- Armed: 
  - If data_in = 0 in the current cycle, data_out must be 1 for that cycle and the machine must enter a terminal Done state.
  - If data_in = 1 at a rising edge, transition back to Idle. In this case, data_out is 0.
- Done: Terminal latch; once entered, the state must never change on subsequent clock edges regardless of data_in, and data_out must remain 0, until rst_n is asserted low.

Output timing:
- data_out is a Mealy output depending on the current state and data_in in the same cycle. It is 1 only in the cycle when the machine is in Armed and data_in = 0. In all other situations, including during reset (rst_n = 0) and in Done, data_out is 0.

question_text:
Design a synchronous RTL module dut that performs an 8-bit division with ready/valid handshakes.

Interface:
- Inputs:
  - clk: clock, rising-edge.
  - rst: synchronous active-high reset.
  - dividend[7:0], divisor[7:0].
  - sign: 1 selects signed operation; 0 selects unsigned.
  - opn_valid: request qualifier.
  - res_ready: consumer ready.
- Outputs:
  - res_valid: result qualifier.
  - result[15:0] = {remainder[7:0], quotient[7:0]}.

Behavior:
- On rst, clear all internal state and drive res_valid=0.
- When idle (no operation in progress and res_valid=0), a request is accepted on a rising clk where opn_valid=1. Latch dividend and divisor at acceptance; ignore further opn_valid until the result is produced and consumed.
- Exactly 8 rising clock edges after acceptance, compute result and assert res_valid=1. While res_valid=1, result must remain stable. res_valid must remain asserted until a cycle where res_ready=1; it must then deassert on the following cycle. A request must not be accepted while res_valid=1.

Division semantics:
- Let |x| denote two’s-complement absolute value for 8-bit x.
- Compute magnitude quotient Qmag and remainder Rmag by dividing |dividend| by (sign ? |divisor| : divisor) with truncation toward zero, ensuring 0 ≤ Rmag < (sign ? |divisor| : divisor). If divisor==0, define Qmag=0 and Rmag=|dividend|.
- Output mapping:
  - If sign=0: quotient=Qmag, remainder=Rmag (both treated as unsigned).
  - If sign=1: remainder carries the sign of dividend (remainder = dividend<0 ? -Rmag : Rmag). The quotient is negated if (dividend<0) OR (divisor<0) (logical OR, not XOR): quotient = ((dividend<0) || (divisor<0)) ? -Qmag : Qmag.
- result = {remainder, quotient} and is only meaningful when res_valid=1.

Note: The sign input must be held constant from acceptance until the result is consumed.

Design a synchronous RTL module that divides an 8-bit dividend by an 8-bit divisor and returns both remainder and quotient with a fixed latency and a valid/ready handshake.

Interface:
- clk: input clock.
- rst: synchronous, active-high reset; clears internal state and deasserts res_valid; any in-flight operation is aborted.
- dividend[7:0], divisor[7:0]: inputs sampled only when a new operation is accepted.
- sign: when 1, perform signed two’s-complement division; when 0, perform unsigned division.
- opn_valid: input indicating a request is present.
- res_valid: output indicating result is available.
- res_ready: input indicating the consumer is ready to accept the result.
- result[15:0]: {remainder[15:8], quotient[7:0]}.

Behavior:
- When idle, on a rising edge where opn_valid=1 and res_valid=0, accept inputs and start exactly one operation (busy thereafter); additional opn_valid assertions while busy are ignored.
- Exactly 8 clock cycles after acceptance, assert res_valid and present the result. res_valid remains asserted until a cycle where res_ready=1; on that cycle the transfer occurs and res_valid must deassert for subsequent cycles. No overlapping operations; a new one may be accepted only when res_valid=0 and the unit is idle.
- Unsigned mode (sign=0): quotient = dividend / divisor; remainder = dividend % divisor.
- Signed mode (sign=1, two’s complement): quotient magnitude = |dividend| / |divisor|, quotient sign = sign(dividend) XOR sign(divisor); remainder magnitude = |dividend| % |divisor|, remainder sign = sign(dividend).
- Division by zero: quotient = 0; remainder = dividend (unsigned) or |dividend| with sign(dividend) (signed).

Output result must be stable while res_valid=1. Only one result is produced per accepted request.

Design a synchronous RTL divider dut with the interface:
- clk, rst (active-high, synchronous)
- dividend[7:0], divisor[7:0]
- sign (0: unsigned mode, 1: signed two’s-complement mode)
- opn_valid (request), res_valid (result valid), res_ready (consumer ready)
- result[15:0] where result[15:8]=remainder and result[7:0]=quotient.

Behavior:
- All state changes occur on the rising edge of clk. On rst=1, the unit becomes idle and res_valid=0; any in-flight operation is canceled. result is only meaningful when res_valid=1.
- A division operation is accepted on a rising edge when opn_valid=1 and the unit is idle (no operation in progress and res_valid=0). The inputs dividend, divisor, and sign are sampled at acceptance.
- Exactly 8 rising clock edges after acceptance, res_valid must assert and result must present the computed remainder and quotient. While res_valid=1, result must remain stable. res_valid remains asserted until a cycle occurs with res_ready=1; it then deasserts on the next rising edge. Requests presented while busy or while res_valid=1 are ignored.

Arithmetic:
- If divisor==0: quotient=0; remainder equals dividend (unsigned if sign=0; two’s-complement if sign=1).
- If sign=0: unsigned division. quotient=floor(dividend/divisor); remainder=dividend−quotient×divisor.
- If sign=1: let a=two’s-complement dividend, b=two’s-complement divisor. Compute q_mag=floor(|a|/|b|) and r_mag=|a|−q_mag×|b|. Output quotient = −q_mag if (a<0) OR (b<0), else +q_mag. Output remainder = −r_mag if (a<0), else +r_mag.

Only one operation may be in flight at a time.

Design a synchronous divider with the following interface:
- Inputs: clk, rst (active-high, synchronous), dividend[7:0], divisor[7:0], sign (0=unsigned, 1=signed two’s complement), opn_valid, res_ready.
- Outputs: res_valid, result[15:0].

Behavior:
- A request is accepted on a rising clk edge when the unit is idle and opn_valid=1 and res_valid=0. On that edge, latch dividend, divisor, and sign and begin processing.
- Compute integer division of dividend by divisor:
  - If sign=0: treat operands as unsigned; quotient = floor(dividend/divisor); remainder = dividend % divisor.
  - If sign=1: treat operands as signed two’s complement; quotient is truncated toward zero; remainder has the same sign as dividend and |remainder| < |divisor| (unless divisor=0).
  - Division by zero: quotient = 0; remainder = dividend (preserving sign when sign=1).

- The detector maintains a deterministic finite automaton that, after each clk rising edge, represents the longest suffix of the input stream seen so far that is also a prefix of the target pattern. The relevant prefixes are: ε, 1, 10, 100, 1001.
- State update on each sampled bit b is as follows (expressed by the longest-suffix rule, unrolled here for clarity):
  - From ε: on b=1 → 1; on b=0 → ε.
  - From 1: on b=1 → 1; on b=0 → 10.
  - From 10: on b=1 → 1; on b=0 → 100.
  - From 100: on b=1 → 1001; on b=0 → ε.
  - From 1001: on b=1 → 1; on b=0 → 10.
- sequence_detected must be high exactly in the same cycle when, after sampling data_in at the clk edge, the updated automaton equals 1001; otherwise low. This produces a 1-cycle pulse and allows overlapping matches (e.g., …11001001… has two pulses).

- After completing an 8-bit word and pulsing dout_valid, no further bits may be captured and no additional dout_valid pulses may occur while din_valid remains continuously high; capturing must resume only after din_valid has been low for at least one full clock cycle.
- dout_parallel updates only in the same cycle dout_valid=1; otherwise it may hold its last value.

Design a synchronous serial-to-parallel converter.

Interface:

- Outputs:
  - dout_parallel[7:0]: the packed 8-bit word.
  - dout_valid: pulses high for one clock to indicate dout_parallel is newly valid.

Behavior:
- Reset: When rst_n=0, immediately clear internal state; after reset, dout_valid=0 and dout_parallel=8’h00.
- Sampling: On each rising edge of clk while din_valid=1, sample din_serial into an 8-bit shift register LSB-first: the first sampled bit becomes bit 0, and each subsequent valid bit shifts existing bits toward MSB and enters at bit 0.
- Burst definition: A “burst” is a maximal contiguous sequence of clock cycles with din_valid=1. Only the first 8 cycles of a burst are sampled; if din_valid=0 on any clock, abandon any partial byte and be ready to start a new burst on the next din_valid=1.
- Output timing: Exactly one clock after the 8th valid sample within a burst, assert dout_valid=1 for one cycle and update dout_parallel to the 8-bit value formed by those 8 samples. On all other cycles, dout_valid=0. When dout_valid=0, dout_parallel must hold its previous value.
- Constraints: Input traffic guarantees din_valid is deasserted at least once between bytes and will not remain high for more than 9 consecutive cycles per burst. Bursts shorter than 8 samples must produce no output.

All behavior is synchronous to the rising edge of clk, except the asynchronous reset.

Design a hardware module dut that converts a gated serial bit stream into 8-bit parallel words with explicit framing and reset behavior.

Interface:
- Inputs: clk, rst_n (asynchronous active-low), din_serial (1-bit), din_valid (1-bit).
- Outputs: dout_parallel (8-bit), dout_valid (1-bit).

Operation:

- input rst_n: active-low asynchronous reset.

  - If state == 2'b00: If wave != 5'b11111, increment wave by 1. If wave == 5'b11111, do not change wave and set state to 2'b01.

module dut
(
  input clk,
  input rst_n,
  output reg [4:0] wave
);

  reg [1:0] state;

  always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
    if(!rst_n) begin
      state <= 2'b10;
    end else begin
      case(state)
        2'b00: begin
          if(wave != 5'b11111) begin
            wave <= wave + 1;
          end else begin
            state <= 2'b01;
          end
        end
        2'b01: begin
          if(wave != 5'b00000) begin
            wave <= wave - 1;
          end else begin
            state <= 2'b00;
          end
        end
        default: state <= state;
      endcase
    end
  end


  always @(negedge rst_n) begin
    if(!rst_n) begin
      wave <= 5'b00000;
    end 
  end


endmodule

Design a synchronous RTL module named dut with the following interface:
- input clk: clock.
- input rst_n: asynchronous, active-low reset.
- output reg [4:0] wave.

Behavior:
- Asynchronous reset (when rst_n=0) must immediately clear wave to 5'b00000. Upon reset, the design must enter an internal “mode” that is not a valid run mode (treat this as a 2-bit code 2'b10). After reset deasserts (rst_n=1), all state changes occur only on the rising edge of clk.

- The design has two valid run modes:
  - Up mode (encode as 2'b00): On each posedge clk, if wave==5'b11111, switch to Down mode and leave wave unchanged that cycle; otherwise increment wave by 1.
  - Down mode (encode as 2'b01): On each posedge clk, if wave==5'b00000, switch to Up mode and leave wave unchanged that cycle; otherwise decrement wave by 1.

- For any mode encoding other than 2'b00 or 2'b01 (including the reset-initialized 2'b10), no registers change on clock edges: wave and the mode must hold their previous values.

Timing/constraints:
- Use a single clocked process sensitive to posedge clk and negedge rst_n.
- No combinational processes or additional outputs.
- wave must never wrap around; at the endpoints 0 and 31, it must plateau exactly one cycle when switching direction.
- Since reset initializes to a non-run mode and no transitions are defined from it, after reset deassertion the module must hold wave at 0 indefinitely.

Implement dut to satisfy the above precisely.

  - Mode 2'b01 (“DOWN”): On each rising edge of clk, if wave != 5'b00000, decrement wave by 1. If wave == 5'b00000, do not change wave on that cycle and switch mode to 2'b00 for subsequent cycles.
- For any other mode value (i.e., not 2'b00 or 2'b01), both wave and the mode must remain unchanged on rising edges of clk (no implicit recovery or wrap-around).
- Reset initialization: The mode must be initialized by reset to 2'b10.

Constraints:

- No additional inputs/outputs are permitted.
- There is no default or combinational behavior beyond what is described above.

Design an RTL module that generates a 5-bit triangular waveform with a synchronous active-low reset.

Interface:
- input clk: clock.
- input rst_n: active-low reset.
- output reg [4:0] wave.

Behavior:
- Reset is synchronous to clk. On any rising edge of clk when rst_n == 0, wave must be set to 0. The internal direction must be initialized to “increasing” so that, after reset is released, counting proceeds upward.
- When rst_n == 1 on a rising edge of clk, wave updates to form a triangular wave between 0 and 31 inclusive with unit steps and endpoint dwell:
  - Increasing phase: if wave < 31, next value is wave + 1. If wave == 31, hold 31 for exactly one additional clock and switch to decreasing phase thereafter.
  - Decreasing phase: if wave > 0, next value is wave - 1. If wave == 0, hold 0 for exactly one additional clock and switch to increasing phase thereafter.
- The output must never wrap (e.g., no 31→0 or 0→31 jumps) and must change only by +1, −1, or 0 (the latter only at the endpoints as specified).
- Changes to rst_n away from clock edges have no immediate effect; they take effect only when sampled on a rising edge of clk.

Example sequence at successive rising edges of clk (after releasing reset): 0, 1, 2, …, 30, 31, 31, 30, …, 2, 1, 0, 0, 1, …

Implement the module with exactly the specified ports and behavior.

Design a synchronous RTL module named dut that generates a 5-bit triangular waveform.

Interface:
- input clk: rising-edge clock.
- input rst_n: active-low reset.
- output reg [4:0] wave.

Behavior:
- Reset semantics:
  - On any rising edge of clk while rst_n = 0, wave must be set to 0.
  - While rst_n remains 0, wave must remain 0 on subsequent rising edges of clk.
  - Changes to wave must occur only on rising edges of clk; deasserting rst_n (returning to 1) must not cause any combinational or non-clocked change.
- Normal operation (rst_n = 1):
  - Starting from wave = 0 after reset, generate a repeating up–down count across the full 5-bit range with single-step updates per clk.
  - The sequence must be: 0,1,2,...,30,31,31,30,29,...,1,0,0,1,2,... and repeat indefinitely.
  - That is, increment by +1 each cycle from 0 up to 31 inclusive; hold 31 for exactly one extra cycle; then decrement by −1 each cycle down to 0 inclusive; hold 0 for exactly one extra cycle; then resume incrementing.
- No wrapping is allowed; the only repeated values are the single-cycle holds at the endpoints 0 and 31.
- The output wave must be fully registered and have no combinational dependence on inputs besides being updated on rising clk edges under the rules above.

Implement only the specified I/O. Internal state may be used but is not exposed.

For example, if the module has just been reset to wave = 0 and direction up, then at the rst_n rising edge wave becomes 1.

Requirements:

- The endpoint “hold then reverse” behavior must be observed exactly as described.

Design a synthesizable RTL module named dut with the following interface:

  - Count up mode: If wave < 31, set wave := wave + 1. If wave == 31, keep wave at 31 for that clock edge and switch the direction to “count down” for subsequent edges.
  - Count down mode: If wave > 0, set wave := wave - 1. If wave == 0, keep wave at 0 for that clock edge and switch the direction to “count up” for subsequent edges.

Design a synchronous square-wave generator.

- inputs: clk (clock), freq[7:0] (unsigned)

Behavior:

- At time 0, wave_out must be 0, and the internal cycle count starts at 0. There is no external reset.
- Let N be the unsigned value of freq interpreted in the range 0–255, with N=0 meaning 256.

  - If freq[7] == 1 on a rising edge (disabled), wave_out must not change on that edge, and the internal cycle count is forced to 0 on that edge.
  - If freq[7] == 0 on a rising edge (enabled), maintain a running count of consecutive enabled clock edges since the last output toggle:

    - Otherwise, increment the running count by 1.

- wave_out must update only on rising edges and must remain constant while disabled.

Implement dut with exactly these ports and semantics.

    - data_out must update to {prev, data_in}, where prev is the most recent data_in sampled on any prior cycle with valid_in=1; if no such prior byte exists since the last reset, prev is 8'h00.
    - valid_out must be 1 if and only if at least one prior valid byte exists since the last reset (i.e., this is the second, fourth, sixth, … valid byte after reset). Otherwise, valid_out=0.
    - The stored prior byte is then updated to the current data_in for future use.
  - If valid_in=0:
    - data_out holds its previous value.
    - valid_out=0.
- Gaps between valid_in assertions do not break pairing; bytes are paired in the order valid_in=1 events occur.
- Examples after reset (A, B, C, D are consecutive data_in values on valid_in=1 cycles):
  - On A: data_out={8'h00, A}, valid_out=0
  - On B: data_out={A, B}, valid_out=1
  - On C: data_out={B, C}, valid_out=0
  - On D: data_out={C, D}, valid_out=1

Design a synchronous RTL module that packs 8-bit tokens into 16-bit words and emits a one-cycle strobe on every second token.

Interface:
- Inputs:
  - clk: system clock.
  - rst_n: active-low asynchronous reset.
  - valid_in: indicates data_in is a token to be captured on this clock edge.
  - data_in[7:0]: input token.
- Outputs:
  - valid_out: strobe indicating a complete 16-bit word is available.
  - data_out[15:0]: output word.

Behavior:
- Reset: While rst_n=0 (asynchronously), the module clears all state, drives valid_out=0 and data_out=0, and forgets any previously seen tokens. After rst_n returns high, counting and accumulation restart.
- Define a “valid event” as a rising edge of clk with rst_n=1 and valid_in=1.
- Let prev denote the most recent data_in captured at a prior valid event since the last reset; if no prior valid event exists, prev=8'h00.
- On every valid event, on the same rising edge:
  - data_out shall be updated to {prev, data_in}, where prev occupies bits [15:8] and data_in occupies bits [7:0].
- If valid_in=0 on a clock edge, data_out shall retain its previous value (no update).
- Index valid events starting at 1 after each reset. valid_out shall be:
  - 1 exactly on valid events with even index (2nd, 4th, …), producing a one-cycle pulse coincident with that event.
  - 0 on all other clock edges, including valid events with odd index and any edge with valid_in=0.

Timing:
- All sampling and updates occur on the rising edge of clk. No additional latency is permitted.

Design a synchronous RTL module that pairs consecutive input bytes into a 16-bit word and emits a one-cycle valid pulse when a pair is produced.

Interface:
- Inputs:
  - clk: clock.
  - rst_n: active-low asynchronous reset.
  - valid_in: single-cycle pulse indicating data_in is valid.
  - data_in[7:0]: input byte.
- Outputs:
  - valid_out: asserted for exactly one clock cycle when a 16-bit output word is produced; low otherwise.
  - data_out[15:0]: most recent produced 16-bit word.

Behavior:
- On the falling edge of rst_n, immediately clear all internal state and set valid_out=0 and data_out=0. After reset deasserts, pairing restarts.
- On each rising edge of clk:
  - Each cycle with valid_in=1 marks arrival of one new byte.
  - The first valid_in after reset (or after completing a pair) is stored but produces no output; valid_out must be 0 and data_out must not change.
  - The second valid_in completes a pair and, in that same cycle:
    - Set valid_out=1 for exactly one cycle.
    - Set data_out to {first_byte, second_byte}, where data_out[15:8]=the earlier stored byte and data_out[7:0]=the current data_in byte.
  - On all other cycles (including when valid_in=0 or when receiving the first byte of a pair), valid_out must be 0 and data_out must retain its previous value.

Additional constraints:
- valid_in is a single-cycle pulse per byte; pulses may be arbitrarily spaced, including back-to-back cycles.
- There is no flow control/ready signal; all state changes occur on posedge clk.
- If an odd number of bytes is received before reset, the last byte is ignored (no output).

Example: After reset deasserts, bytes A, B, C, D arrive on four valid_in pulses across cycles. Outputs: {A,B} with a one-cycle valid_out, then {C,D} with a one-cycle valid_out. No other outputs occur.

Design a Verilog RTL module dut with the following interface:
- input clk: rising-edge clock
- input rst_n: asynchronous, active-low reset
- input valid_in: qualifies input data
- input [7:0] data_in: input byte
- output reg valid_out: qualifies output word
- output reg [15:0] data_out: output word

Behavior:
- Reset: While rst_n=0, valid_out=0 and data_out=0. Any partial state is cleared immediately. After rst_n returns high, operate from a clean state on the next clk edge.
- Input capture: On each rising edge of clk when valid_in=1, sample data_in.
- Pairing: The module forms 16-bit words from pairs of sampled bytes, in arrival order. For each pair, the earlier byte becomes data_out[15:8], and the later byte becomes data_out[7:0].
- Output timing: When the second byte of a pair is sampled (i.e., on the clk edge with the second valid_in=1 since the previous output or reset), assert valid_out=1 for exactly that cycle and update data_out to the concatenation {earlier, later}. On all other cycles, valid_out=0 and data_out must not change.
- Gaps: Cycles with valid_in=0 do not alter any internal state; incomplete pairs persist across such gaps.
- Streaming: For a run of consecutive valid_in=1 cycles, outputs occur on every second such cycle, producing words from bytes (1,2), (3,4), etc.
- Reset during an incomplete pair discards the pending first byte.

Example: If valid_in=1 with data_in=A, then later valid_in=1 with data_in=B (no reset between), valid_out=1 and data_out={A,B} on the B cycle.

Implement only the specified behavior; no additional handshaking or latency is permitted.

Design a byte-pair packer with the following interface:
- Inputs: clk (clock), rst_n (asynchronous active-low reset), valid_in, data_in[7:0]
- Outputs: valid_out, data_out[15:0]

Behavior:
- Reset: When rst_n is 0, all internal state and outputs must be cleared immediately (asynchronously). valid_out must be 0 and data_out must be 0. After rst_n returns to 1, the next valid_in=1 marks the start of a new pair.
- Sampling: On each rising edge of clk, data_in is sampled only if valid_in=1.
- Pairing and output:
  - Treat successive assertions of valid_in as forming pairs; cycles with valid_in=0 are ignored (they do not reset pairing and do not count toward a pair).
  - The first valid byte of a pair is stored but produces no output.
  - On the second valid byte of that pair, assert valid_out=1 for exactly that clock cycle and set data_out to {first_byte, second_byte}, with first_byte in data_out[15:8] and second_byte in data_out[7:0].
- On any cycle that does not emit a pair, valid_out must be 0. data_out must retain its previous value unless a new pair is emitted.

Example (after reset deasserts): if valid/data are (1,A), (0,x), (1,B), (1,C), (0,x), (1,D) on successive clk edges, then outputs pulse on the 3rd and 6th edges:
- Edge 3: valid_out=1, data_out={A,B}
- Edge 6: valid_out=1, data_out={C,D}
All other edges: valid_out=0; data_out unchanged.

Implement the module named dut with the exact I/O above.

Design a Verilog module dut with the following interface:
- input clk: system clock.
- input rst_n: asynchronous active-low reset.
- input valid_in: indicates data_in is valid this cycle.
- input [7:0] data_in: input byte.
- output reg valid_out: status indicating “second-byte phase.”
- output reg [15:0] data_out: concatenated output word.

Behavior:
- Reset: On any negedge of rst_n, asynchronously clear all internal state and outputs to 0. While rst_n=0, valid_out=0 and data_out=0.
- Pairing protocol: The module groups input bytes (data_in when valid_in=1) into ordered pairs and outputs a 16-bit word {first_byte, second_byte}.
- Phase control:
  - The module maintains a two-state phase initialized to “first-byte phase” after reset.
  - On each rising edge of clk, if valid_in=1, the phase toggles; if valid_in=0, the phase holds.
- Data handling:
  - When in first-byte phase and valid_in=1 at a rising edge, latch data_in as the first byte (no change to data_out).
  - When in second-byte phase and valid_in=1 at a rising edge, update data_out to {latched_first_byte, data_in}.
  - In all other cases, data_out retains its previous value.
- valid_out reflects the current phase each cycle: it is 1 whenever the module is in second-byte phase and 0 otherwise, independent of valid_in. Thus, after accepting a first byte, valid_out remains 1 across any number of idle cycles (valid_in=0) until the next valid byte is accepted, after which the phase returns to first-byte phase.

All behavior is synchronous to posedge clk except the asynchronous reset.

Design a synchronous RTL module that assembles incoming 8-bit bytes into 16-bit words over two arrivals.

Interface:
- clk: rising-edge clock.
- rst_n: active-low asynchronous reset.
- valid_in: when high on a rising edge, data_in holds a new byte to consume.
- data_in[7:0]: input byte.
- valid_out: status/output indicator (registered).
- data_out[15:0]: concatenated output word (registered).

Behavior:
- Asynchronous reset: When rst_n=0 (at any time), immediately clear all state: no pending byte is stored; valid_out=0; data_out=0. After rst_n returns high, operation restarts expecting a first byte.
- On each rising clk edge with rst_n=1:
  - If valid_in=1 and there is no pending first byte, latch data_in as the first byte of a pair. Do not change data_out. valid_out shall be 0 in this cycle and 1 in subsequent cycles until the pair is completed.
  - If valid_in=1 and there is already a pending first byte, produce data_out = {first_byte, data_in} in this same cycle. valid_out shall be 1 in this cycle. The pending state is cleared so the next byte (if/when received) will start a new pair.
  - If valid_in=0, retain any pending first byte; data_out must not change.
- Concatenation order: data_out[15:8] equals the earlier (first) byte; data_out[7:0] equals the later (second) byte.
- Timing of valid_out: valid_out is high in every cycle after capturing a first byte and before the second byte arrives, and also high in the cycle the second byte arrives; it is low in all other cycles, including the cycle that captures a first byte.

Bytes may be back-to-back or separated by arbitrary gaps; behavior must be consistent across gaps.

Design a synchronous module that aggregates incoming 8-bit samples into 16-bit words using a phase bit. The interface is:
- clk: clock
- rst_n: asynchronous active-low reset
- valid_in: when 1, data_in carries a new 8-bit sample on this rising edge
- data_in[7:0]: input sample
- valid_out: registered indicator
- data_out[15:0]: registered output word

Behavior:
- Asynchronous reset: When rst_n=0, immediately clear all internal state and outputs to 0. On the first rising edge with rst_n=1, operation resumes from cleared state.
- Maintain a 1-bit phase p, initialized to 0 by reset. On each rising edge:
  - If valid_in==1, toggle p; if valid_in==0, p holds.
  - If valid_in==1 and p was 0 just before the edge, latch data_in into an internal upper-byte register.
  - If valid_in==1 and p was 1 just before the edge, update data_out to {latched_upper, data_in} (latched byte as [15:8], current input as [7:0]).
  - If no update occurs, data_out holds its previous value.
- valid_out is a registered signal that, on each rising edge, equals 1 iff p was 1 just before that edge; otherwise 0. Note: valid_out may assert even when valid_in==0.

Timing notes:
- All sampling and updates occur on rising edges of clk; “p was X just before the edge” refers to the value from the prior cycle.
- Example: After reset, if valid_in=1 for two consecutive cycles with inputs A then B, then on the second cycle valid_out=1 and data_out={A,B}. If there is a gap after A, the next cycle still asserts valid_out=1, but data_out updates only when a subsequent valid_in=1 occurs with p previously 1.

Implement exactly this behavior.

Design a synchronous “byte packer” that groups incoming 8-bit samples into 16-bit words. Implement a module with the following interface:
- Inputs: clk (clock), rst_n (active-low asynchronous reset), valid_in (1-bit), data_in (8-bit).
- Outputs: valid_out (1-bit), data_out (16-bit).

Behavioral requirements:
- All state updates occur on the rising edge of clk.
- When rst_n is 0, the design must asynchronously clear: valid_out = 0, data_out = 0, and any internal state so that the next valid byte is treated as the first of a new pair.
- When valid_in = 1 at a rising edge, data_in is accepted. The design shall pack every two accepted bytes into one 16-bit word: the earlier (first) byte becomes data_out[15:8], and the later (second) byte becomes data_out[7:0].
- On the exact clock cycle that the second byte of a pair is accepted (i.e., the pair is completed), valid_out must be 1 for that cycle, and data_out must equal {first_byte, second_byte}.
- In all other cycles, valid_out must be 0.
- data_out must update only when a pair is completed; otherwise it must retain its previous value.
- If only one byte of a pair has been accepted so far, no output is produced yet; that byte must be stored internally until a subsequent cycle with valid_in = 1 provides the second byte. Periods with valid_in = 0 do not discard the stored first byte.
- If valid_in = 1 for many consecutive cycles, outputs occur every second cycle for pairs (0,1), (2,3), etc., in order.

No backpressure or overflow behavior is required beyond this sequencing.

Design an RTL module that packs incoming 8-bit bytes into 16-bit words using a simple valid-only interface.

Interface:
- clk: system clock; all sequential activity occurs on the rising edge.
- rst_n: asynchronous active-low reset; when 0, all registers and outputs are cleared to 0 and pairing restarts.
- valid_in: when 1 at a rising edge, the byte on data_in is accepted.
- data_in[7:0]: input byte to be accepted when valid_in=1.
- valid_out: asserted for exactly one clock cycle when a 16-bit word is produced.
- data_out[15:0]: output word; updates only when valid_out=1 and otherwise holds its last produced value.

Behavior:
- The module accepts every byte on each rising edge where valid_in=1; there is no backpressure/ready.
- Bytes are paired in arrival order. The first accepted byte of a pair becomes data_out[15:8], and the second accepted byte becomes data_out[7:0].
- On the rising edge where the second byte of a pair is accepted, valid_out must be 1 and data_out must present the concatenation {first_byte, second_byte}. On all other cycles, valid_out must be 0.
- Pairing state persists across idle cycles (valid_in=0). If a single byte is accepted and then there is a gap, the next accepted byte completes the pair and produces an output.
- If an odd number of bytes are accepted before reset, the last unpaired byte is held internally and only contributes when the next byte arrives; upon reset, any partial pair is discarded.
- When rst_n=0, valid_out must be 0 and data_out must be 0. After rst_n returns to 1, pairing restarts with the next accepted byte as the high byte of a new pair.

Implement the module per the above specification.

Design a synchronous RTL module dut that packs incoming 8-bit samples into 16-bit words in order, emitting an output only after every second accepted byte.

Interface:
- input clk: clock; all sampling occurs on rising edges.
- input rst_n: asynchronous active-low reset. When rst_n is 0, all state and outputs are cleared immediately; after rst_n returns high, pairing restarts from the first byte.
- input valid_in: when 1 at a rising edge, data_in is accepted as the next byte in the sequence; when 0, no byte is accepted.
- input [7:0] data_in: byte to accept when valid_in=1.
- output reg valid_out: pulses high for exactly one clock cycle when a 16-bit word is produced; 0 otherwise.
- output reg [15:0] data_out: holds the most recently produced 16-bit word; updated only on cycles when valid_out=1; otherwise retains its previous value (or 0 after reset).

Behavior:
- The module consumes each asserted valid_in byte in arrival order. It pairs bytes 1&2, 3&4, 5&6, etc., regardless of idle cycles between them.
- On accepting the first byte of a pair, no output is produced yet. On accepting the second byte of that pair, set valid_out=1 for that cycle and set data_out to {first_byte, second_byte}, with first_byte in data_out[15:8] and second_byte in data_out[7:0].
- If rst_n is asserted low at any time, any partially collected first byte is discarded, valid_out becomes 0, and data_out becomes 0. After reset deassertion, the next accepted byte is treated as the first of a new pair.

Assume no backpressure or ready signals; valid_in is the sole qualifier.
